Shares of Bajaj Finance dropped around 3% on Wednesday after the company reported a 29% year-on-year increase in net profit to Rs 6,367 crore for the July-September quarter of the ongoing financial year 2027.
 Bajaj Finance on Monday released its results for Q2 FY27, reporting a 24% YoY increase in net interest income (NII) to Rs 13,335 crore during the quarter under review, from Rs 10,785 crore reported in the year-ago period. The company’s assets under management (AUM) grew 26% YoY to Rs 5.85 lakh crore. The stock dropped to Rs 929.20 apiece on NSE on Wednesday morning.
The non-banking financial company booked 13.45 million new loans in the second quarter, up 11% from 12.17 million reported in the corresponding period last year. Its customer franchise grew 16% YoY to 128.85 million as of September 30, adding 4.42 million customers during the quarter.
 Also read | Bajaj Finance Q2 Results: Net profit jumps 29% YoY to Rs 6,367 crore, NII up 24% 
 Nomura on Bajaj Finance share price 
Nomura maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on the shares of Bajaj Finance with a target price of Rs 1,270 apiece, implying nearly 33% upside potential in the stock’s previous closing price of Rs 957.35 apiece on NSE.
 Live Events
The international brokerage said the NBFC’s net profit was in line with its estimate, but 3% behind consensus. Its credit cost of 1.56% was lower than estimated. Growth momentum in all segments has been healthy, and in line with expectations till September 2026. The MSME book should grow in a double-digit range in the second half of FY27, as per management estimates, it added.
Given the rising rate environment, Bajaj Finance’s management has indicated marginal headwinds on NIMs. “We trim EPS estimates by 2-3% and expect ROA and ROE of 4.2% and 19.9% over FY28-29. We assume the capital raising to be completed in FY27F itself,” Nomura added.
 Jefferies on Bajaj Finance share price 
Jefferies maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on the shares of Bajaj Finance but reduced its target price to Rs 1,230 apiece from Rs 1,280 apiece. The international brokerage said that company’s profit was in line with estimate. While stressed loans saw a slight rise from gold loans, management sees a negligible impact and confirmed that asset quality stays strong. 
Clarity on flexi-loans & banca fees will be watched and management is taking mitigating steps, Jefferies said. “We marginally trim estimates and see 25% Cagr in profit over FY26-29. BAF stays among our top- picks,” Jefferies added.
 360 One WAM on Bajaj Finance share price 
 360 One WAM upgraded its rating on the shares of Bajaj Finance from ‘Hold’ to ‘Buy’, with a target price of Rs 1,150 apiece. This implies more than 20% upside potential from the stock’s previous closing price.
The domestic brokerage said Bajaj Finance delivered NII in line with estimates, while lower-than-expected fee income resulted in a marginal miss on PPOP and PAT. Growth remained the key highlight, with AUM expanding 26.5% YoY, prompting management to raise its FY27 growth guidance to 26-27% from 22-24% earlier. Accordingly, 360 One WAM has upgraded its growth estimates for FY27-28. 
Overall, the brokerage believes that Bajaj Finance delivered a strong quarter, supported by healthy growth, positive demand commentary and prudent risk management. “We have factored in capital infusion and warrant conversion over FY27-28, resulting in a higher book value but lower estimated RoE of 20% versus 22% earlier…Following the recent correction and the resulting improvement in risk/reward, we upgrade the stock to Buy from Hold,” it said.
 Also read | Why is market rising today? Sensex jumps 800 points, Nifty above 23,050. Key factors behind D-Street rebound 
 Bajaj Finance share price 
Bajaj Finance shares have fallen more than 6% in a month and around 2% in 2026 so far, with the stock overall down 12% in one year.
Over the longer term, the shares of the non-banking financial company delivered positive returns of more than 23% in three years and 24% in five years. The company has a market capitalisation of more than Rs 5.96 lakh crore.

docs.title: Walmart launches tools for AI agents to shop for customers
docs.text:
Synopsis
 Walmart on Wednesday intrduced new tools that will allow artificial intelligence agents to shop and complete transactions for customers, as the retailer seeks to position itself in the growing use of AI-powered assistants in online commerce.
 Listen to this article in summarized format
 Listen 
 Walmart on Wednesday intrduced new tools that will allow artificial intelligence agents to shop and complete transactions for customers, as the retailer seeks to position itself in the growing use of AI-powered assistants in online commerce.
The move underscores Walmart's push into AI-enabled shopping, and strikes a contrast with Amazon, which has sought to limit third-party AI shopping agents' access to its platform.
Here are the details: 
* The retailer said it will roll out "Agent Profiles" next month, enabling shoppers to authorize individual AI agents, track their purchases separately and set spending limit or require approval for each transaction
* Walmart said customers would be able to monitor purchases made by AI agents separately from their own orders and revoke agent access at any time
* The tools instilled confidence in the "experimental" shopping process of agentic purchases, said Mizuho analyst David Bellinger in a note
* "... the momentum and buy-in from top management teams seems to be making this into a real thing," Bellinger added.
* The company also launched the " Walmart Agent Gateway ," a platform that allows AI assistants such as OpenAI's ChatGPT, Google's Gemini and Meta's Muse to connect directly with Walmart and Sam's Club systems to search products and complete purchases
* Walmart said customers would remain in control of purchases, while AI agents would be barred from accessing payment card data and could be blocked for violating company rules
* The company said the tools will be available to all Walmart account holders and will not require a Walmart+ membership

docs.title: Dassault’s solo Rafale F5 push could reshape India’s fighter plans
docs.text:
India’s long-running hunt for 114 new fighters has taken on a fresh complication. As the Indian Air Force weighs its next big procurement, a key design decision in France could narrow the options available to New Delhi for the next decade and more. 
According to defence.in , Dassault Aviation has chosen to develop the Rafale F5 entirely on its own, a move that could push export availability of the upgraded jet to around 2035. That timeline matters because India’s expected assembly line for the 114 Multi-Role Fighter Aircraft, or MRFA , would likely be locked into producing the current Rafale F4 or F4-plus standard well before the F5 becomes available. 
 Why the F5 is not just another upgrade 
The Rafale F5 is being positioned as a substantial leap rather than a routine refresh. It is intended to bring deeper sensor fusion, stronger electronic warfare performance and more secure connectivity, while also allowing the aircraft to operate alongside uncrewed combat aerial vehicles. In practical terms, that places the programme much closer to the logic of a 5th-generation ecosystem than a conventional mid-life update. 
 That distinction is important for India because the MRFA competition has been shaped by the need for a large, locally built fleet rather than a short-term import buy. A fighter that arrives too late in the production cycle, even if it is more capable, may not fit easily into a manufacturing plan already built around a different configuration. 
 What Dassault’s timeline means for India 
 The strategic concern is less about whether the Rafale F5 will be attractive and more about when it will be ready for export customers. If the aircraft is not mature enough for overseas sales until about 2035, then India’s production line for the MRFA order could already be deep into F4-plus output by then. Retooling an Indian assembly ecosystem for a new standard midway through a 114-jet programme would be expensive, technically complex and disruptive to supply chains. 
 That is why the earlier assumption, that India could simply mix a small number of future F5 aircraft into a much larger Rafale fleet, now looks far less realistic. Once factories, vendors and quality-control processes are calibrated for one standard, shifting to another is rarely a simple matter of software or minor hardware changes. It would require a different production strategy, new integration work and likely a fresh commercial negotiation. 
 The industrial logic behind the MRFA contest 
The MRFA programme is not just about buying a capable aircraft. It is also tied to India’s push for domestic manufacturing under the Make in India framework. France has already submitted a technical and commercial proposal for the 114 jets, and that offer is understood to include significant participation for Indian industry. For New Delhi, the appeal of the Rafale has always rested partly on combat performance and partly on the possibility of building a large share of the fleet at home. 
If production begins in the early 2030s, however, the industrial path will likely be set around the Rafale F4-plus standard. That would still deliver a highly capable 4.5-generation platform, but it would also mean the Indian line is unlikely to transition quickly into the more advanced F5. The result is a choice between near-term operational readiness and longer-term technological edge. 
 France’s fighter roadmap is shifting too 
The French side of the equation is also changing. France is increasingly banking on the Rafale F5 as a central pillar of its future air-power strategy, particularly after reports in June 2026 that the Franco-German Next Generation Fighter project had been cancelled because of industrial disputes. If that broader European effort remains stalled, the Rafale F5 becomes even more important for Dassault’s long-term combat aircraft roadmap. 
That makes the company’s decision to pursue development without foreign partners significant for export markets as well. A solo programme may give Dassault greater control over design and delivery, but it also appears to stretch the timeline for international buyers. For India, that means the F5 may remain a future possibility rather than an immediate procurement option. 
 What India can still gain from the deal 
Even with the F5 horizon pushed back, the Rafale F4-plus remains a strong answer to the IAF’s urgent needs. It offers a mature combat platform, proven multirole capability and an upgrade path that is already well understood. In a force structure facing pressure from ageing aircraft and squadron shortages, that matters more than waiting indefinitely for a next-step variant that may not fit the current procurement timetable. 
The more difficult question is whether India should treat the F5 as a distant follow-on or as a reason to keep the MRFA process open longer. Either way, Dassault’s decision changes the bargaining landscape. The IAF can still pursue a large Rafale order, but it now has to do so knowing that the aircraft most closely associated with 5th-generation features will not arrive early enough to be folded smoothly into the same production run. 
For policymakers, that is the central trade-off. The immediate fleet gap can be addressed with the current-generation Rafale. The more advanced drone-carrying F5, however, is likely to remain a later chapter in India’s fighter modernisation story rather than part of the first act.

docs.title: DRDO taps private firms for India’s first indigenous 20mm helicopter gun
docs.text:
India’s push to localise frontline weapons has moved into a new phase with a helicopter gun programme that could reshape the country’s aviation armament base. The Armament Research and Development Establishment , or ARDE, a DRDO laboratory, has picked SSS Defence and Kalyani Group as development-cum-production partners for a home-grown 20mm turret gun system, according to raksha-anirveda.com . 
 A first for India’s combat helicopter armament 
The project is significant not only because it adds another indigenous defence item to the pipeline, but because it targets a capability India has not previously built end-to-end at home. The medium-calibre aviation gun under development would be the first of its kind to be fully designed and manufactured in the country, marking a departure from long-standing dependence on imported helicopter weapons. 
 That matters for more than symbolism. In combat aviation, a turret gun is not a niche accessory. It is a core close-support weapon used for suppressing hostile positions, protecting troops on the ground and engaging targets in difficult terrain and low-altitude operations. A domestically sourced system also gives the armed forces more control over spares, upgrades and ammunition supply, areas where imported platforms can become vulnerable to delays and export controls. 
 Why Rudra and Prachand need a local alternative 
The new gun is intended for Hindustan Aeronautics Limited ’s Advanced Light Helicopter Mk-IV-Rudra and the Light Combat Helicopter , known as Prachand. These helicopters currently use the French-made THL-20 turret fitted with European M621 cannons. Replacing or supplementing that setup with an Indian system would deepen the operational self-reliance of both platforms and reduce exposure to overseas supply chains. 
 For India’s rotary-wing fleet, the move also fits a broader procurement pattern. The armed forces have increasingly sought to align combat capability with domestic design and production, not just to cut import dependence but to create a stable industrial base for upgrades, life-cycle support and future exports. In that context, a locally developed turret gun is as much an industrial programme as it is a weapons project. 
 Two private firms, one production pathway 
The development plan outlined for the programme gives the selected partners a two-year window to complete design work, testing and user acceptance. Once the prototype clears trials, production will be split between the two companies, with the final workload determined through competitive bidding. 
 Under the proposed model, the lower bidder will receive 60 per cent of the manufacturing order, while the other partner will take the remaining 40 per cent. That structure is designed to keep pressure on costs while still preserving competition between the two industrial teams. It also gives the programme a built-in hedge against bottlenecks by avoiding dependence on a single supplier. 
 What the shortlist says about India’s defence ecosystem 
The choice of SSS Defence and Kalyani Group points to a wider shift in how India is trying to build complex military hardware. Instead of relying solely on a public sector prime, the programme brings in private industry at the development stage itself, giving domestic manufacturers a larger role in design, qualification and serial production. 
 For the defence ecosystem, that could have lasting consequences. A successful 20mm helicopter gun programme would not only create a new line of indigenous ordnance but could also strengthen confidence in private-sector participation for other aerospace and weapons projects. It would add depth to the supply chain, support ancillary manufacturing and potentially open a route to exportable systems if the product meets performance and reliability benchmarks. 
India’s drive for self-reliance in defence has often been measured by large-ticket platforms such as aircraft, submarines and armoured vehicles. Yet smaller subsystems can be equally strategic because they determine whether a platform can be sustained in service without external dependence. In that sense, the helicopter gun programme is a test case for whether the country can indigenise not just the headline equipment, but the critical components that make those platforms combat-ready. 
 From import dependence to domestic control 
The practical payoff of the programme could be substantial if the development schedule holds. A home-grown gun and ammunition chain would reduce the vulnerability of India’s attack helicopters to geopolitical shocks, supply interruptions and pricing pressure from foreign vendors. It would also simplify long-term maintenance planning for the armed forces, which increasingly need predictable access to parts, barrels, mounts and ammunition stocks over the full life of a platform. 
The initiative is also likely to be watched closely by defence manufacturers looking for signals on future procurement philosophy. If the model works, it may encourage more programmes where design responsibility, production capacity and cost competition are all located within India rather than split across foreign suppliers and local assemblers. 
For now, the shortlist itself is the key milestone. The project is still at the development stage, but it represents a notable step toward an indigenous helicopter weapon system that could eventually sit at the centre of India’s combat aviation arsenal. If the programme delivers as planned, it will do more than replace an imported gun. It will show that India can build a complete medium-calibre aviation weapon chain, from design to production, within its own industrial base.

 A missing date of death or incorrect citizenship information might seem like a small administrative error but inaccurate records can complicate how government agencies verify identities and manage benefits. Social Security Administration is now working to address those gaps by correcting nearly 50 million records in what it calls "the most comprehensive SSN record clean up in the agency’s 91-year history."
 The agency said that the changes are intended to improve the accuracy of its database and help prevent improper payments across government programs.
So the announcement may leave Social Security recipients wondering whether the corrections could affect their monthly checks. The SSA has not announced any automatic benefit increases or cuts tied to the cleanup and the number of records corrected does not show how many beneficiaries, if any, will see a change in their payments. 
 What the SSA Found in Its Records
The cleanup covers several types of missing or inaccurate information.
The Social Security Administration has added 17 million dates of death to records that previously lacked them. Drawing on information from its internal systems and the Department of State.

The SSA updated about 25 million records with missing citizenship information using data from Department of Homeland Security’s Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements service, as per an announcement on Tuesday.
Then another 8.5 million records containing inaccurate citizenship status information are still being corrected.
Taken together, since the beginning of the Trump Administration, the work covers nearly 15% of active Social Security numbers, according to the agency. The SSA has also introduced stronger internal controls to reduce errors caused by manual data entry.
These corrections are intended to make records more reliable. They should not be confused with a count of fraudulent claims or improper payments.
 You Might Also Like: 
 Ursula Burns was ready to leave Xerox for Dell. Then one phone call changed her career path
 Could Your Monthly Social Security Payment Change
The cleanup does not amount to a new change in Social Security benefits . SSA has not said that retirees, disabled workers or other recipients will automatically receive more money or have their payments reduced because of the initiative.
The agency said that its records help federal and state agencies verify identities and prevent improper payments. More accurate information can help those agencies administer government programs using reliable records.
The announcement does not explain how many of the corrected records were connected to benefit payments, nor does it identify recipients whose payments have changed as a result.
That means beneficiaries should not assume that a record correction will affect their checks as the available figures do not give a direct link between the cleanup and a change in any individual's benefits.
 You Might Also Like: 
 A Student introduced Mark Hatala to Nvidia before the AI boom. His initial $2,000 investment led to a stake worth over $1 million by 2024
 US Social Security Administration database cleanup
 Why Accurate Social Security Records Are Important
Different government agencies depend on SSA records "to validate identities and prevent improper payments of taxpayer dollars," as per SSA. That's why missing death dates can leave records incomplete and missing/ inaccurate citizenship information can create gaps in information available for verification.
Commissioner Frank J. Bisignano said, “The Social Security Number database is our country’s books and records. The database’s accuracy is essential to maintaining integrity of government services for citizens. Accurate SSN records prevent fraud across federal programs and support the proper administration of benefits.”
Bisignano added that, “This is the first time SSA has undertaken an effort of this scale, and I am proud of the work we have done to strengthen the foundation of identity data relied upon throughout government and the economy.”
 What Beneficiaries Need to Know Right Now
The SSA has not announced a new payment schedule or a general change to eligibility rules as part of this cleanup. It has also not said that every beneficiary must take action because records are being corrected.
The remaining work includes correcting 8.5 million records with inaccurate citizenship status information but the agency has not provided a completion date.
The agency is correcting information used to administer government programs, but it has not announced that those corrections will automatically change monthly benefits.
Whether an individual is affected will depend on the details of their record and how the corrected information is used. The total number of records updated, by itself, cannot tell a beneficiary whether their payment will change.

docs.title: What to Donate on Papankusha Ekadashi? 5 Items, Traditions and Their Religious Significance
docs.text:
Papankusha Ekadashi is observed by devotees of Lord Vishnu through fasting, prayers and acts of charity. Donating essential items on this day is considered an expression of devotion, generosity and compassion. From food grains and clothes to fruits and other daily necessities, devotees can choose donations according to their means and local traditions.
 What to Donate on Papankusha Ekadashi? 
 1. Food Grains and Essential Food Items 
Donating rice, wheat, pulses and other staple foods is a traditional way to support people facing food insecurity. Devotees may offer these items to families in need, community kitchens or charitable organisations.
 2. Clothes 
Donating clean clothes, particularly to people who need them, is associated with compassion and helping others meet basic needs. Choose usable garments appropriate for the recipient and the season. 
 3. Fruits and Other Food Items 
Fresh fruits and suitable food items can be donated to people in need or offered through religious and charitable institutions. Ensure that all food is fresh, hygienically handled and appropriate for the recipients.
 4. Water and Basic Necessities 
Providing drinking water and essential daily-use items is another practical way to mark the occasion through charity. Donations should address genuine needs rather than follow a costly or elaborate ritual.
 Live Events
 5. Donations for Religious or Charitable Causes 
Devotees may contribute money or useful supplies to temples, community kitchens or charitable organisations. Such donations should be voluntary and within one's financial capacity.
 Significance of Charity on Papankusha Ekadashi 
Charity on Papankusha Ekadashi reflects the values of generosity, selflessness and service associated with Hindu religious observances. Devotees believe that acts of giving, performed with sincere intentions, support spiritual discipline and express devotion to Lord Vishnu.
The type and method of donation can vary by family, region and religious tradition. There is no need to make an expensive contribution; helping someone meet a genuine need is a meaningful way to observe the spirit of charity.
Refer to our main Papankusha Ekadashi, October 22, 2026 guide for Date, Tithi, Parana Time, Vrat Katha, Puja Vidhi and Significance
 How to Make Donations on Papankusha Ekadashi 
 Choose useful items that meet the recipient's needs.
 Give voluntarily and according to your financial capacity.
 Ensure donated food, clothes and other goods are clean and suitable for use.
 Consider supporting a trusted charity, community kitchen or local initiative.
 The central message of donating on Papankusha Ekadashi is generosity with sincerity. A thoughtful contribution that helps someone in need can be a practical expression of the day's devotional spirit.

docs.title: Karwa Chauth 2026: 7 Bollywood Celebrity Looks to Inspire Your Festive Wardrobe
docs.text:
Karwa Chauth is the perfect occasion to bring out your favourite sarees, embroidered suits and traditional jewellery. As women prepare for the festival on October 29, 2026, Bollywood celebrities offer plenty of inspiration for creating a festive look that feels elegant, glamorous and personal. From classic silk sarees and statement blouses to richly embroidered Anarkalis and contemporary kurta sets, there are several ways to dress up for the occasion without buying an entirely new outfit.
 Whether you prefer a traditional red ensemble or want to experiment with jewel tones, pastels and contemporary silhouettes, these seven celebrity-inspired Karwa Chauth outfit ideas can help you plan your festive wardrobe. The key is to adapt the colours, fabrics and styling details to suit your comfort, budget and personal taste.
 Also Read: Karwa Chauth 2026 Moonrise Time: When Will the Moon Be Visible in Delhi, Noida, Mumbai and Other Cities? 
 1. Alia Bhatt-Inspired Saree Look: Elegant and Understated 
 Alia Bhatt showcases festive elegance in a fuchsia-pink saree with gold detailing and a contrasting turquoise-blue blouse, offering inspiration for Karwa Chauth 2026 outfit ideas. (Source: Alia Bhatt’s Instagram)
Alia Bhatt's traditional saree appearances offer inspiration for women who prefer understated elegance over heavily embellished outfits. For a recent festive appearance, she wore a fuchsia-pink saree with gold detailing and a turquoise-blue puff-sleeved blouse, demonstrating how contrasting colours can create a striking traditional look.
For Karwa Chauth, recreate this style with a pink, magenta or red saree featuring delicate gold embroidery. Pair it with a contrasting blouse, gold jhumkas and a few bangles. A neat bun, a small bindi and soft makeup can complete the look without making it feel overdone.

docs.title: Sharad Purnima 2026: Purnima Vrat Vidhi and Satyanarayan Katha, Muhurat and Samagri
docs.text:
Sharad Purnima falls on Sunday, October 25, 2026. According to the Drik Panchang for New Delhi, the Purnima Tithi begins at 11:55 AM on October 25 and ends at 9:41 AM on October 26. The exact timings may vary slightly by location.
 Devotees planning to perform Satyanarayan Puja should confirm the suitable puja time with their local Panchang, particularly if they intend to perform the ritual in the evening. The appropriate timing can depend on the observance followed and the local tithi calculations.
 Read More: Sharad Purnima 2026 Date: October 25 or 26? Check Moonrise Time, Purnima Tithi and Kheer Ritual 
 Purnima Vrat Vidhi: How to Observe the Fast 
Devotees can follow these steps to observe the Purnima Vrat according to their family traditions.
 Take a bath and make a sankalp: Begin the day with a bath and resolve to observe the fast with devotion. Keep the puja area clean and arrange the necessary materials.
 Prepare the puja space: Place an idol or picture of Lord Vishnu or the deity you traditionally worship on Purnima. Arrange flowers, a diya, incense and other offerings.
 Offer prayers: Worship the deity with flowers, roli, akshat, fruits and other customary offerings. Chant prayers or Vishnu mantras according to your practice.
 Observe the fast: Follow your family's customary fasting rules. Practices may differ, with some devotees observing a strict fast and others consuming permitted foods.
 Perform the evening rituals: If observing the traditional evening worship, offer prayers at the appropriate time. Those performing Satyanarayan Puja can complete the katha, aarti and prasad offerings as part of the ritual.
 Complete the vrat: Follow your customary method of concluding the fast. Devotees who observe Satyanarayan Puja generally receive panchamrit and prasad after the aarti.
 Satyanarayan Puja Samagri: Complete Checklist 
Keep the following items ready before beginning the puja. Requirements may vary according to regional customs and the instructions followed by the family priest.
 Live Events
 For the altar: Puja chowki, clean cloth and an idol or picture of Lord Vishnu or Satyanarayan.
 For kalash and worship: Kalash, water, mango leaves where customary, roli, kumkum, akshat and sandalwood paste.
 For offerings: Fresh flowers, garland, fruits, bananas, betel leaves and supari.
 For the aarti: Diya, cotton wicks, ghee or oil, incense sticks and camphor.
 For panchamrit: Milk, curd, honey, ghee and sugar.
 For Satyanarayan prasad: Ingredients for the customary sheera or panjiri, such as wheat flour, sugar, ghee and bananas, depending on the recipe followed.
 For the katha: A Satyanarayan Katha book or printed text.
 Additional items: Tulsi leaves, a plate for offerings and clean utensils for preparing prasad.
 Check the list before starting the puja to avoid interruptions during the ritual.
 Satyanarayan Puja Vidhi: Step-by-Step Procedure 
Satyanarayan Puja is dedicated to Lord Vishnu in his Satyanarayan form. It is commonly performed on Purnima and other occasions considered auspicious by devotees.
 1. Prepare the altar and take a sankalp 
Clean the puja area and place the idol or picture of Lord Satyanarayan on the prepared chowki. Arrange the kalash and other puja materials according to your family's tradition. Begin with a prayer and take a sankalp to perform the puja.
 2. Worship Lord Satyanarayan 
Offer flowers, sandalwood paste, roli, akshat, fruits and other customary items to the deity. Light the diya and incense. Offer panchamrit where prescribed by the puja tradition, using clean utensils and following the appropriate ritual procedure.
 3. Prepare the prasad 
Prepare the customary Satyanarayan prasad, often made with ingredients such as wheat flour, ghee, sugar and banana. Some families prepare sheera, while others follow different regional recipes. Keep the offering ready for the concluding part of the puja.
 4. Recite the Satyanarayan Katha 
Read or listen to the Satyanarayan Katha with the family and other participants. The traditional narration describes the origin and observance of the vrat through stories that emphasise devotion, truthfulness, gratitude and keeping one's promises.
Participants traditionally listen to the katha as part of the puja. Keep the text ready beforehand so the recitation can proceed without interruption.
 5. Perform the aarti and distribute prasad 
Conclude the puja with the aarti of Lord Satyanarayan. Offer the prepared prasad and panchamrit according to the family's custom, then distribute them among the participants. Devotees observing the fast may consume prasad as part of their customary vrat completion.
 What to Keep in Mind During Purnima Vrat 
 Fasting rules: The type and duration of the fast can vary. Follow your customary practice and consider individual dietary needs.
 Puja timings: Check a location-specific Panchang before finalising the ritual schedule.
 Samagri requirements: Some ingredients are optional or region-specific. Confirm any special requirements with your family priest.
 Satyanarayan Katha: Keep the text ready and arrange the puja materials in advance.
 Prasad preparation: Prepare the offering hygienically and distribute it after the ritual according to tradition.
 Sharad Purnima provides an occasion for devotees to observe the full-moon vrat and worship Lord Vishnu through Satyanarayan Puja. Preparing the samagri in advance, checking the local muhurat and following the customary ritual sequence can help families organise the observance smoothly.

As preparations for the Union Budget 2026–27 gather pace, the groundwork underway signals a clear policy intent to accelerate domestic demand, revive private investment and generate employment, according to a budget note by Motilal Oswal Financial Services (MOFSL). The brokerage has identified five stocks across auto, agriculture, defence, financials and infrastructure themes, which it believes could deliver strong gains for investors.
 "The Budget is expected to focus on income-tax, GST, and customs simplification to enhance ease of doing business and support fiscal consolidation, alongside targeted support for agriculture, MSMEs, manufacturing, infrastructure, higher defence capex, EVs, and renewables through credit and incentives," the note authored by Research Analysts Sneha Poddar and Rekha Jaat said.
A strong capital expenditure thrust across highways, logistics, defence, rail freight corridors and connectivity is anticipated, complemented by emphasis on skilling, rural prosperity, women empowerment, AI adoption, climate action and digital finance to anchor India’s next phase of economic expansion, the note added.
The finance ministry started work on the Union Budget for 2026-27 from October 9 as per a circular issued by the Department of Economic Affairs (DEA).
The preparations come against the backdrop of an additional 50% US tariff on most Indian goods and other external headwinds. These have raised risks to India's growth and jobs outlook, prompting calls for stronger support to the export sector.
 Live Events
 5 stocks to buy: 
The stocks recommended by MOFSL are TVS Motor Company, UPL , Bharat Dynamics (BDL), M&M Financial Services and Dalmia Bharat , and each of these stocks has been assigned a 20% weight.
 1) TVS Motors: TVS Motors continues to outperform peers and is well-positioned to benefit from the budget’s push to boost domestic consumption and rural demand through higher allocations, income support, and infrastructure spending.
MOFSL said that improving rural sentiment, strong entry-level recovery and sustained two-wheeler demand will be key triggers. Moreover, the company's market share gains, easing discounts, and margin expansion will provide strong earnings visibility. The Apache and Ntorq maker remains its top pick in OEMs.
 2) UPL: The diversified agrochemical leader is well positioned to benefit from the union budget push riding on rural prosperity via higher agri credit, MSME support, and value-chain strengthening, lifting farmer incomes and crop-protection demand.
The company's strong points are stronger volumes, export tailwinds, improved working-capital discipline and post-bond-repayment balance-sheet strength, the brokerage note said. The company's rising focus on speciality chemicals supports solid 2HFY26 growth.
 3) Bharat Dynamics: Bharat Dynamics (BDL), a defence play, has a robust Rs 50,000 crore order pipeline over five years, with Rs 20,000 crore targeted in 2-3 years. This aligns with the expected defence capex surge and infra push.
The recent Rs 2.5 lakh crore DAC approvals for missiles, undersea warfare, and naval arms leverage BDL's tactical/strategic expertise, propelling FY31 turnover to Rs 100bn via indigenisation and lower provisions, the note said.
 4) M&M Financial Services: M&M Financial is poised for Union Budget 2026-27 benefits via rural prosperity, MSME credit, and employment focus, driving PV/tractor loan growth amid surging volumes from festive demand, GST cuts, and restocking.
The company targets Rs 3 lakh crore in assets under management (AUM) by 2030, which is at an 18-20% CAGR, bolstered by AI underwriting, lower credit costs, controlled opex, and margin stability for strong earnings visibility in retail portfolios.
 5) Dalmia Bharat: The cement company benefits from the budget’s infra capex surge, PMAY rural housing, and urban projects, driving cement volume growth.
Dalmia Bharat is a low-cost cement producer with high blending ratios, green power and low freight. The company is targeting 62 mtpa capacity by FY28, and its cost optimisation endeavours will likely lift EBITDA margins amid sector consolidation.

Reliance Power 's board of directors on Monday approved the issuance of up to 46.20 crore equity shares/warrants worth Rs 1,525 crore via preferential allotment mode.
 The board has set the issue price at Rs 33 per share.
The issue price of equity shares/warrants is at a discount of 13% over Monday's closing price of Rs 38.15 on the NSE. The announcement was made after market hours and Reliance Power shares on Monday ended with gains of Rs 1.81 or 4.98% over the previous closing price.
 Reliance Infrastructure Limited, the promoter of the company, will enhance its equity stake by over Rs 600 crore, a company filing said. The other investors in the preferential issue are Authum Investment and Infrastructure Limited and Sanatan Financial Advisory Services Private Limited.
The proceeds from the preferential issue will be utilised to expand business operations directly and/or through investment in subsidiaries and joint ventures, debt reduction and for general corporate purposes, the filing said.

The markets worldwide are waiting with bated breath on what will be a historic policy announcement from the US Federal Reserve , where the central bank is expected to usher in a rate cut cycle.
 The announcement will be made at 11:30 pm IST (Indian Standard Time) on Wednesday.
If analysts are to be believed, the US Fed is all but certain to cut interest rates for the first time in more than four years.
However, there is no consensus on the quantum of reduction. Some are predicting a smaller cut of a quarter of a percentage point, while others believe a bigger half-point reduction is in the works.
Senior officials at the US central bank, including Powell, have indicated that a rate cut is coming, as inflation eases toward the bank's long-term target of 2%, and the labour market continues to cool in the post-Covid economy.
 Live Events
If the Fed starts the rate cut cycle, the Reserve Bank of India is also expected to follow suit.
A smaller cut would be a more predictable move, while a bigger cut would do more to boost demand — while also running the risk of reigniting inflation.
 WATCH LIVE TODAY: Press conference with #FOMC Chair Powell at 2:30 p.m. ET: https://t.co/1uJrua5qsH https://t.co/FJa6TbkDMt pic.twitter.com/87g5NJITsz 
— Federal Reserve (@federalreserve) September 18, 2024 
By the end 2024, markets are expecting a total reduction of at least 100 basis points in the first rate cut cycle in over 4 years since 2020.
But whether the Fed goes for 25 or 50 bps, the biggest trigger for stock prices to move up or down would be Powell's motivation behind the cut.
Asset classes from stocks, currencies and fixed income could all log swings in the immediate aftermath of the Fed decision.
While easing US interest rates are directionally positive for equities in general, “we should keep in mind interest rates are just one variable in a complex adaptive system that determines the direction of Indian equity markets”, said Anoop Vijaykumar, Investments and Head of Research at Capitalmind.

Nomura has maintained its 'Buy' rating on Piramal Finance with a target price of Rs 2,550, naming it its top pick among non-banking financial companies (NBFCs) under its coverage. The brokerage said the lender's healthy operating trends, reduction in its legacy book and management's confidence in achieving a return on assets under management (ROAUM) of 2.5% by the fourth quarter of FY27 support its positive view.
 Piramal Finance reported a 67% year-on-year increase in net profit to Rs 5.4 billion in the second quarter of FY27, supported by 24% growth in total assets under management (AUM) and 30% growth in retail AUM. The legacy book declined 32% sequentially and accounted for 1.5% of total AUM as of September 2026.
Credit costs remained benign at 1.1% on an annualised basis in the quarter, while net slippages as a percentage of opening loans were at their lowest in 11 quarters. Net interest margins (NIMs) expanded by only 2 basis points sequentially, as yields were affected by the lower number of days in the second quarter compared with the first.
 Rising interest rates unlikely to pressure margins 
Nomura said management does not expect the rising interest rate environment to drag down NIMs, with Piramal's credit rating upgrade in the fourth quarter of FY26 and the run-down of its legacy book expected to provide protection.
"Thus, despite having over 50% of the book in floating rate assets, it does not see the need to hike its customer lending rate," Nomura said, referring to management's assessment.
The brokerage added that Piramal's rupee bonds maturing over the next 10 quarters have yields of 8.5%-10.8%, and said it remained comfortable with its NIM estimates.
 Asset quality largely stable, mortgage stress persists 
Nomura said asset quality trends in the growth book remained largely stable. Gross Stage 2 assets declined by 18 basis points sequentially, while Gross Stage 3 assets rose by 7 basis points.
The brokerage noted that early signs of stress in the mortgage book, previously flagged by management among borrowers employed in the IT sector in southern India, persisted in the second quarter of FY27, although the stress remained geographically restricted.
In the digital loan segment, rolling 90-plus days past due (DPD) in the 12-month-on-book portfolio rose by 10 basis points sequentially. Management believes the company is well protected, with 90% of the book covered by a first loss default guarantee (FLDG).
Nomura continues to build in a 2.9% ROAUM for the lending business in its FY29 estimates, compared with management's optimism about reaching 2.5% by the fourth quarter of FY27.
"Maintain Buy and SOTP-based TP of INR2,550," the brokerage said, adding that the stock trades at a one-year-forward price-to-book value of 1.4 times.

 Nomura initiates Acme Solar with Buy, target price Rs 505.
 NTPC Green Energy rated Neutral with target price of Rs 100.
 Energy storage seen as critical for India's grid stability.
 Did our AI summary help? 
 Market Mastery
Nomura has initiated coverage on Acme Solar Holdings with a 'Buy' rating and a target price of Rs 505, and on NTPC Green Energy with a 'Neutral' rating and a target price of Rs 100, identifying energy storage as a critical technology to address the challenges arising from rising renewable energy penetration in India's electricity mix.
India's renewable capacity, excluding hydro, grew from 46 GW in FY16 to 223 GW in FY26, supported by renewable energy resources, government policies and declining tariffs. The share of renewable energy in power generation rose from around 1% in FY06 to 17% in FY26.
 However, the increased share of renewable energy is creating grid-level challenges, including falling thermal utilisation during the day, peak usage at night and curtailment of solar generation.
"The increased RE share in India's electricity mix is leading to issues such as grid instability and a mismatch in the timing of power generation and consumption, as there are variability and intermittency issues related to renewables," Nomura said.
"Energy storage has become necessary, to resolve the issue of oversupplied solar energy during the day and to utilize it during non-solar hours and, thus balancing the renewable power scale," the brokerage said.
 The share of grid storage-backed tenders rose from 22% in FY22 to 87% in FY26. Nomura said energy storage also helps in "maintaining grid stability, frequency and improving grid flexibility implied through a planning reserve margin".
Nomura said Acme Solar "is transitioning from a conventional solar IPP to a firm, dispatchable platform". It expects the company's revenue and EBITDA to grow at CAGRs of 66% and 65%, respectively, over FY26-FY29F.
 The brokerage expects growth to be driven by "the commissioning of firm & dispatchable renewable energy (FDRE) projects which have high equity IRRs", along with declining battery energy storage system (BESS) prices and the early commissioning of storage capacity.
Nomura said the company could commission BESS capacity independently in merchant and short-term markets "to drive equity returns", with a target of installing 25 GWh of BESS capacity.
Of Acme Solar's total portfolio of 8.4 GW, 5.4 GW remains under execution, with power purchase agreements signed for 4.3 GW of capacity. Nomura said this "improves growth visibility, in our view".
The brokerage initiated coverage with a 'Buy' rating and a target price of Rs 505, based on "a one-year forward EV/EBITDA of 10.2x on Dec'28 EBITDA".
 NTPC Green: 'Neutral', target price Rs 100 
Nomura expects NTPC Green Energy s revenue and EBITDA to grow at CAGRs of 74% and 72%, respectively, over FY26-FY29F.
The brokerage said growth would be driven by a "strong pipeline underpinned by 16GW of awarded capacity and MoUs it has signed with other PSUs or state entities". It also noted that, as a sovereign-backed entity, the company "benefits in terms of lower cost of debt than peers".
NTPC Green plans to install around 34 GWh of BESS capacity and contract pumped storage projects (PSP), which Nomura believes "will help in its next structural shift to RE".
However, the brokerage flagged execution risks, saying: "We believe NGEL will face execution delays due to tight transmission availability, and we conservatively factor in lower capacity additions vs. company guidance."
Nomura initiated coverage on NTPC Green with a 'Neutral' rating and a target price of Rs 100, based on "a one-year forward EV/EBITDA of 13.3x on Dec'28 EBITDA".

Shares of Bajaj Finance fell nearly 3% on Wednesday as investors weighed the lender's September-quarter performance against concerns over margin pressure from rising interest rates, even as brokerages maintained positive ratings and target prices of up to Rs 1,300.
The stock fell to Rs 925.60 on the NSE at 12:54 pm on Wednesday, down 3.32%.
 Bajaj Finance reported a 29% year-on-year increase in net profit to Rs 6,367 crore for Q2FY27. Net interest income (NII) rose 24% year-on-year to Rs 13,335 crore from Rs 10,785 crore in the year-ago period, while assets under management (AUM) grew 26% to Rs 5.85 lakh crore. Here’s what brokerages are saying:
HSBC said Bajaj Finance's "segment-leading performance continues" and that "MSME loan growth [is] likely to revive".
The brokerage said "multiple levers [are] available to offset revenue headwinds and protect RoA/RoE in FY28-29". It added that a potential capital raise could support growth and profitability.
Nomura said Q2FY27 net profit was "in-line with estimates". It noted that the company had raised its FY27 loan growth guidance to 26-27%, while keeping its medium-term guidance unchanged at 23-25%.
The brokerage expects the credit cost run-rate in H2FY27 to "match H1FY27", but cautioned that "rising rates could create marginal NIM headwinds".
Nomura cut its FY28-29 earnings per share estimates by 2-3% and expects return on assets (RoA) and return on equity (RoE) of 4.2% and 19.9%, respectively. It said the stock trades at 3.4 times one-year forward price-to-book value.
JPMorgan: Overweight | Target price: Rs 1,260
JPMorgan highlighted a strong second quarter, with NII rising 24% year-on-year to Rs 13,330 crore, pre-provision operating profit (PPoP) increasing 21% to Rs 10,700 crore and profit after tax (PAT) growing 29% to Rs 6,270 crore.
The brokerage said the revised FY27 loan growth guidance of 26-27% reflected "strong business momentum". It described asset quality as "benign", with "only transient stress in short-tenure gold loans".
JPMorgan also highlighted the company's "focus on protecting RoA despite higher funding costs & NIM risks". It called Bajaj Finance a "best-in-class earnings compounder", citing loan growth, AI-led operating leverage and credit-cost management, and expects a 21% earnings CAGR over FY27-29.
CLSA: Outperform | Target price: Rs 1,300
CLSA said Q2FY27 profit before tax was "in-line, 4% above estimates after adjusting for a Rs 340 crore macro-economic provision".
The brokerage noted that AUM growth accelerated to 26% year-on-year from 24% in Q1FY27, while FY27 growth guidance was raised by 3-4 percentage points to 26-27%. PPoP "slightly exceeded estimates", and the net slippage ratio declined 110 basis points year-on-year, indicating stronger asset quality.
CLSA said interest rate swaps had supported funding costs, but management had "flagged margin pressure from rate hikes". It also noted that an equity raise was planned to fund growth and address leverage exceeding five times. The brokerage added that there were "no specific details yet" on how the impact of insurance guidelines would be offset.

 Indian equities gave up a strong opening and ended lower on Wednesday, the first session after the Dussehra holiday, as heavy selling in midcap and smallcap stocks overshadowed IT gains. Nifty 50 fell 77.60 points, or 0.34%, to close at 22,811.35, after rising to 23,120.90 in early trade, while Sensex slipped 143.21 points, or 0.19%, to settle at 73,709.69. 
 Sentiment was upbeat at the open as positive global cues and the launch of the Jio Platforms IPO, expected to be India's largest, encouraged buying. However, investors booked profits at higher levels, while Brent crude remained above $110 per barrel amid tensions around the Strait of Hormuz, keeping market sentiment cautious. 
 The broader market bore the brunt, with Nifty Smallcap 100 falling about 2.5% and the midcap index declining nearly 2%. IT was the biggest gainer, gaining about 2%, led by Infosys, Tech Mahindra, TCS, and HCL Tech. Bajaj Finance, Eternal, Eicher Motors, Nestle, and Trent were among the biggest losers, while Autos, Chemicals, and Financials also weighed. Breadth was deeply negative, with 608 stocks advancing, 2,988 stocks declining, and 102 remaining unchanged. Investors will track the Jio IPO subscription and quarterly earnings.

docs.text:
Mint Money 
 Dinner with strangers, ₹1,500 a ticket: the economics of India’s at-home social clubs
 Ann Jacob 6 min read 21 Oct 2026, 12:42 PM IST 
 Summary
 From supper clubs to themed game nights, home-hosted events are becoming a paid social space. Attendees seek meaningful connections, while hosts balance ticket prices, costs and profitability. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 On a Saturday evening in Bengaluru, 39-year-old author and educator Divya Ramachandran sat in a stranger’s living room as the host dismantled his collection of vintage wristwatches to explain how they work. On other weekends, she has shared poetry, attended African instrument showcases and joined a “PowerPoint hour”, where guests present on random topics they are passionate about over a potluck meal.
 In Kochi, 26-year-old software engineer Prasannath attended house gatherings to share meals with strangers who have similar interests, hoping to overcome social anxiety and build friendships.
 Across metros and Tier-II cities, at-home events and workshops are becoming a micro-economy. Hosts turn flats and terraces into pop-up cafés, murder mystery arenas, ice cream swaps and supper clubs. Amid urban isolation, some people are redirecting discretionary spending from crowded commercial venues towards curated gatherings, paying for the prospect of meaningful connections.
 Beyond outings
 For attendees, cafés and restaurants can mean higher food costs and distractions that hinder conversations.
 “The majority of social events in Bangalore are outdoors in cafés or restaurants, where the connections made with people fizzle out,” said Divya. “At home events, there are no distractions, and there is space to focus on conversations. I have made more genuine friends than at outdoor social events.”
 Divya allocates ₹ 15,000-20,000 a month to discretionary spending, from which she funds at least one at-home event every weekend. Although she has encountered overpriced ₹ 3,000 events that lacked value, she views well-curated gatherings as a worthwhile investment in a dependable community.
 Prasannath caps his monthly event spending at ₹ 3,000-4,000. “House events are an unexplored concept,” he said. “Intimacy is what people look forward to. Prices around ₹ 500 - 1,500 are acceptable to access this third space and improve your social life, considering how isolated our lives have become.”
 Attendees note that there is a premium in the ticket prices as hosts open their own doors, but as the spread of variety and space for connections based on shared interests grows, they do not hesitate to pay the premium, as long as they are able to make lasting connections.
 The host’s math
 While attendees weigh value for money, hosts must manage setup costs, pricing and brand partnerships. For some, hosting has become a full-time profession; for others, it remains a passion project.
 Sandhya Verghese, a 31-year-old experience curator in Kochi, started with a ₹ 499 “Kanji and unlimited papadam” night in her apartment. She later turned her three-bedroom flat into a café for a day, converting her bedroom into a coffee-brewing room and another room into a bakery.
 “I started lean with very little profit margin because I bore most of the costs myself,” Verghese shared.
 Her ticket prices have since risen from ₹ 499-2,200 in India to ₹ 7,000 for an event in Dubai. To keep gatherings accessible in a Tier-II market while controlling costs, she uses reusable DIY décor and brand partnerships.
 “Brand deals help reduce my costs, allowing me to redirect my budget toward interactive details. What started as a secondary income stream has now become my full-time work,” she said. She supplements her earnings with stand-up shows and work as a digital marketing consultant.
 But saving on venue rent does not guarantee profits. Shivank Goel, a 25-year-old product manager and content creator, founded Yellow Club, a community built around themed gatherings at home. Its events range from Harry Potter experiences and murder mysteries to childhood-themed activities and custom matching-app gatherings. After starting in Delhi, he has moved the project to Bengaluru.
 Despite charging ₹ 1,499-1,999 per ticket, the venture does not make a profit.
 “The biggest misconception is that hosting at home is automatically profitable because you don’t pay for a venue,” Goel explained. “Decor is expensive for themed events. You save on renting a space, but you still have to account for materials, food, drinks, cleaning, cancellations, marketing , and your own time and effort. For me, it’s an experiment in whether social experiences can become a sustainable business.”
 Running Yellow Club alongside his full-time job of being a product manager and content creator, Goel sets event-specific spending limits and tries to break even.
 Community costs
 Simoni Sahoo, a 30-year-old product enablement consultant in Bangalore, invested ₹ 50,000-1,00,000 for initial setup costs of buying cushions, plates, and decor to create a women-first community space on her terrace. She also has a monthly recurring spend of ₹ 15,000-20,000 on refreshing supplies. Her ticket prices range from ₹ 700 for board game nights to ₹ 3,500 for supper clubs.
 “People are paying for exclusivity, curation, and the fact that it feels like a home,” Sahoo explained. Brand deals provide additional income, but profitability is not her immediate goal. “It is not profitable at this moment for me. For me, it’s about building a community based on shared interests.”
 Addressing how she manages the financial risk, Sahoo explained: "The initial setup of the space definitely came from my main income, and the first month of events was also largely self-funded as an initial investment. Since then, I’ve been making the events as self-sustaining as possible."

docs.text:
Mint Money 
 Bonding with bonds: high yields possible, but be mindful of the risks
 Joydeep Sen 5 min read 21 Oct 2026, 02:13 PM IST 
 Summary
 Double-digit bond yields can be attractive, but investors should remember that higher returns come with higher credit and default risks. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 In bond investments, there are high-credit-quality bonds with single-digit returns and investment-grade bonds with double-digit returns. High-credit-quality bonds are government bonds or AAA-rated corporate bonds. Investment-grade is a technical term; it refers to bonds rated BBB and above. There is a credit rating scale moving from AAA to AA to A to BBB; the definition of investment grade is based on this. For high-credit-quality bonds, you can go through the mutual fund route, or do it yourself (DIY) through online bond platforms. For high-yield investment-grade bonds, there are products from Portfolio Management Services (PMS) and Alternative Investment Funds (AIFs), but for bigger ticket sizes. Or you can DIY through online bond platforms.
 When you go through the morning newspapers and see cover-page ads screaming about attractive double-digit returns, it has to be seen in perspective. Return and risk go hand in hand; returns come from risk. When you are going through a high-yield fund offered by an AIF or investments curated by a PMS, a fund manager conducts due diligence on the bond issuers. When you are DIY, you may not have the bandwidth to do the research and understand the risks. The full-page ad showcasing lucrative returns has been put up by a Securities and Exchange Board of India ( Sebi )- registered entity, but it has no accountability if and when the issuer defaults. To be fair, in a mutual fund or AIF or PMS, the fund manager would not pay you from their pocket in case of default. However, they have their goodwill at stake. For a professional fund manager, a default tarnishes the image. When you are going for high-risk river rafting, you would rather have a professional guide on your boat.
 There is a risk of a communication gap here; let us cite two examples. The ad states that these are secured bonds. ‘Secured’ is a nice-sounding word, but digging into what it means—it means a charge against the assets of the issuer. These are physical assets, e.g., land, buildings, or machinery. You would feel happy: in case the issuer defaults, you have access to these assets. However, in that event, you cannot just sell the underlying assets—you have to go to court. Once a suit starts, how long it will take to get settled and how much you will recover are anyone’s call. Second example. It is mentioned that these are credit-rated bonds. But you have to look at the credit rating —is it AAA or BBB? For all you know, it could even be below investment grade, i.e. below BBB. You have to have your antennae up, particularly when you are DIY.
 Sebi consultation paper 
 The grey areas and borderline issues regarding the loud advertisements mentioned earlier bring us to one relevant aspect. On 21 August 2026, Sebi issued a Consultation Paper on Advertisement Code for Online Bond Platform Providers (OBPPs). Certain provisions in the paper merit a highlight, if you are DIY, for risk assessment:
 “It has been observed that advertisements increasingly utilize behavioural prompts, urgency-based messaging and promotional techniques that may encourage investors to take investment decisions without adequate due diligence. Accordingly, it is considered necessary to address advertisements that create artificial scarcity, Fomo or otherwise induce investors to make hurried investment decisions”. Self-explanatory.
 “Standard warning in legible fonts which states “Fixed returns are not guaranteed returns. Investments in debt securities are subject to market, credit and default risks.” Since people have a bank fixed-deposit mindset towards all fixed-income investments, including market-linked ones, this is important.
 “OBPPs are permitted to utilize the phrases such as “Returns are predictable” or “Passive Income”, “market volatility” etc., which touch upon the nature of the debt securities. These phrases shall be used in a generic, non-promissory manner, supported by adequate risk disclosures, appropriate disclaimer as prescribed”. Note that fixed income investments are predictable, unlike equities, but there is no guarantee.
 “Adjectives such as high yield, high rated, high returns and synonyms of such words, which are vague and general without any basis shall be avoided”. This is important. What is high rated and what are higher returns is subjective and open to debate.
 If you are going with a fund manager, you can check pedigree and track record. If you are DIY, or do not have the ticket size for PMS/ AIF, you need to be careful about tall claims.
 Joydeep Sen is a corporate trainer (financial markets) and author.

docs.title: Iran’s fleet of shadow tankers has run out of oil after monthslong US blockade
docs.text:
Global 
 Iran’s fleet of shadow tankers has run out of oil after monthslong US blockade
 Jon Emont , The Wall Street Journal 4 min read 22 Oct 2026, 06:57 AM IST 
 Summary
 Tehran had millions of barrels of crude in tankers floating in Asian waters that gave it a steady flow of much-needed cash. Now, that oil has dried up. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 For most of the war, Iran had an invaluable cushion: dozens of oil tankers holding millions of barrels of crude sitting safely in waters in Asia. Tehran steadily sold the oil to China, bringing in billions of much-needed cash.
 Now, that floating storage is gone. By mid-October, the reserves were fully depleted, according to analysts at Kpler, as a U.S. naval blockade prevented Iran from replacing the crude it normally sells to Chinese refineries.
 “There’s no more oil to discharge to China anymore,” said Homayoun Falakshahi, head of crude-oil analysis at Kpler.
 The drop in oil revenue is a further blow to Iran’s struggling economy, already facing runaway inflation and widespread shortages. U.S. Central Command, which is responsible for the Middle East, said Saturday that the blockade has denied Tehran at least $25 billion worth of oil revenue, which will, in turn, constrict Iran’s ability to replace destroyed factories and weapons.
 U.S. actions have “imposed devastating costs on Iran’s security apparatus,” said Adm. Brad Cooper, head of U.S. Central Command.
 Even as the U.S. pressure has choked off Iranian exports, oil from elsewhere in the Middle East is flowing, recently exceeding prewar levels, as U.S. protection helps secure the passage of non-Iranian oil through the Strait of Hormuz.
 The floating storage has been part of an elaborate system Iran developed over the years to get oil to its main customer, China, despite U.S. sanctions.
 Instead of sending oil directly to Chinese refineries, tankers linked to Iran ferried the crude to waters off the coast of Malaysia and Singapore. They then transferred the oil to other tankers that transported it to Chinese refineries. The subterfuge made it harder for the U.S. to track the flow of oil and punish sanctions violators. The waters off Malaysia and Singapore also became a useful place to store oil.
 Oil analysts say Chinese payments for Iranian oil can take around two months to arrive, meaning Tehran may still receive a trickle of funding from past sales in the weeks ahead.
 Iran has defied predictions that the blockade would collapse its economy and squeeze concessions on its nuclear program for more than six months. Tehran has stored oil in derelict tanks and trucked it to neighbors as the sea route shuts down.
 Still, the overall picture is grim for Iran’s economy. Falakshahi says oil sales represent around 30% to 40% of Iran’s government revenue and are its largest source of foreign exchange. A weakening Iranian currency, which has fallen by a third against the dollar since early July, is contributing to breakneck inflation.
 “It looks like the U.S. gamble is that the economy will either push the regime back into negotiations to accept a nuclear deal, or will spark protests internally which the regime will face challenges containing,” Falakshahi said.
 Alternative routes to export Iranian oil that don’t go through the Strait of Hormuz, like trucking oil overland, won’t come close to replacing the oil transported by sea, according to analysts.
 “Is it working? Yes, it’s working,” said Iman Nasseri, senior vice president of Middle East and Asia at energy-analytics company FGE NexantECA in Dubai, who once worked in the research arm of Iran’s oil ministry. Still, he said the regime has proven resilient in the past. “Let’s wait another year and see if the system can stand.”
 According to Kpler, by the start of the war in February, Iran had around 135 million barrels located overseas—much of it off the coast of Malaysia and Singapore—likely worth around $10 billion or more after the price of oil surged. When the U.S. first imposed a blockade on Iranian oil flows in April, Iran continued selling oil from this offshore reserve, with stores declining rapidly.
 When the U.S. lifted the blockade as part of peace negotiations in mid-June, Iran rushed out more oil, building back its reserves until the U.S. reimposed the blockade in mid-July. Those reserves, which had peaked at nearly 90 million barrels, fell to less than 1 million barrels by Oct. 5, and have since been completely exhausted, according to Kpler.
 Emma Li, an analyst at energy tracker Vortexa, also reported a major drop, estimating that there were about 6 million barrels of Iranian oil off Singapore as of Oct. 9. She said Chinese oil refineries are increasingly turning to alternative suppliers, including Brazil and West Africa.
 United Against Nuclear Iran, an advocacy group, also calculated that Iran’s oil exports had fallen to close to zero in August and September and that floating reserves in Southeast Asia had likely fallen to 10 million barrels or less by early October, saying the precise total was difficult to know. “They’ve got to be hurting,” said Charlie Brown, a UANI researcher. He said that while he couldn’t say that the reserves had gone to zero, “it seems likely to be well on the way to close to zero.”
 Iran’s government insists it can withstand the pressure. At a meeting of the International Monetary Fund in Bangkok last week, Abdolnaser Hemmati, governor of Iran’s central bank, said that despite pressure “the Iranian economy has demonstrated very good resilience, and the claim that Iran’s economy is collapsing is nothing more than an illusion.”
 Write to Jon Emont at jonathan.emont@wsj.com

docs.title: French protests can be traced to weak fiscal management—and therein lies a lesson
docs.text:
Opinion 
 French protests can be traced to weak fiscal management—and therein lies a lesson
 Mint Editorial Board 3 min read 21 Oct 2026, 07:31 AM IST 
 Summary
 The question that an over-indebted France must answer is whether its government can get its fiscal house in order. As credit gets costlier not just across the euro-zone but globally, fiscal responsibility assumes all the more importance. If at all, only the US can breathe easy. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 As student protests sweep across France, it is easy to dismiss it as familiar if uniquely French stuff. But at the bottom of it is something that’s increasingly common to governments all over: fiscal profligacy. 
 A redux of the Greek crisis of 2009-10 might seem distant, but as unrest spreads beyond French borders, it is time to examine if there are any lessons for us. 
 At the root of the problem is France’s inability to get its fiscal house in order. On the face of it, the protests echo concerns of India’s ‘cockroach’ stir over education: dilapidated classrooms, poorly run state schools, and so on. 
 But there the similarity ends. 
 Unlike in India, where years of lectures from multilateral institutions made economic policymakers wary of running high fiscal deficits, rich countries of the West had no such qualms. 
 Inevitably, the chickens are coming home to roost. Investors have begun treating France as the ‘sick man of Europe,’ with a debt-to-GDP ratio of almost 120% (in contrast with India’s 80% odd). 
 In France’s case, its yawning deficits and debt overload are chiefly an outcome of its inability to curb a rapidly rising pension bill. Paris has long been aware of this, but every time an administration tried to reform the system, it was forced to retreat. The net result is that many of its youth are condemned to a future of slower growth, strained public services and a welfare system far less supportive than it once was. 
 Add the country’s political chaos, with candidates on the far right and hard left vying to win its presidency next year, and the French stage seems set for months of turbulence that could spill across the wider euro-zone. 
 The question that France must answer—and a show of police force does not count as one—is whether it can exercise fiscal restraint. Consider: France’s budget deficit exceeds 5% of its GDP, which is more than India’s gap of 4.4% last year and this year’s target of 4.3%, and leaves very little space for finding extra cash to satisfy the needs of students. 
 As signs of discontent erupt in Belgium, Portugal, Spain and Albania, the EU could face a severe test. The EU’s Growth and Stability Pact, which limits national fiscal deficits to 3% of GDP, was designed partly for cohesion to enable a common currency, the euro. 
 Today, it exists only on paper, but the euro-zone has a unified monetary authority that recently hiked its policy rate to tackle inflation. Dearer credit affects all of Europe , but French bonds stand out for their rising yields and risk premia, which make it particularly expensive for Paris to borrow funds for public spending. 
 Given an oil shock amid an AI boom, costlier capital is a global trend. The US, whose debt pile has also grown enormous, has two key advantages. 
 One , its economy’s growth is robust—thanks largely to AI—and not weak like France’s. Two , the US dollar’s status as a trade and reserve currency spells vast global demand for its bonds, which lets America run outsized deficits year after year. Since this is not true of other countries, the sooner they recognize it and act accordingly, the better. 
 In any case, US yields have been hardening too, and it’s unclear if this is just a war blip, given how an AI investment cycle going beyond data centres could keep interest rates ‘higher for longer’ (if overall savings are unable to keep up). 
 With credit no longer cheaply available and the future uncertain on multiple fronts, no country can afford to relax its fiscal vigil.
