docs.text:
Global 
 Europe’s dependence on America in space is hard to escape
 The Economist 6 min read 21 Oct 2026, 06:33 PM IST 
 Summary
 The EU plans to spend €15bn ($17bn) on IRIS 2, a constellation of 348 communications satellites to be used by its members’ governments and armed forces. But the first will be launched only in 2029. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 THE STRONGEST signals that America is turning against Ukraine have come, this month, from outer space. Ukrainian drones’ connections to Starlink, Elon Musk’s satellite-internet service, cut out at speeds above 160kph. Russian ballistic missiles smacked into Kyiv without the usual warnings from American spy satellites. Ukraine’s European allies reacted with deep foreboding. European defence chiefs can offer Ukraine only partial substitutes for American intelligence and communications networks. And they worry about their own dependence on America’s space-based capabilities, about whether these will stay available if Russia attacks and about how quickly they can develop their own alternatives.
 All this is hastening efforts to develop alternatives. The day after Ukraine said restrictions had been placed on Starlink, shares in its closest European competitor, Eutelsat, surged by 23%. The European Union then moved to speed up the glacial pace of regulatory approval for merging the satellite-making businesses of three large European aerospace companies, hoping to create one big enough to compete with Mr Musk’s SpaceX. And on October 19th four of the region’s largest telecommunications firms said they wanted to partner with a satellite company to compete with Starlink.
 Yet Europe has a long way to go before it can hope to achieve “autonomy in space”, as the jargon has it. In three crucial areas, it depends on America. The first is satellite-internet service for civilians and the armed forces. The second is space-based intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance (ISR) and early warning for defence. And the third is launch capacity: the rockets and spaceports needed to put a large number of satellites into orbit.
 For decades, the space gap between Europe and America was widest in defence. America kept Europe dependent in part by letting its allies freeload on programmes such as SBIRS, an $18bn missile-warning constellation. But America also opposed Europe’s efforts to develop its own capabilities. It initially tried to block Galileo, a satellite navigation system, on the grounds that it would compete with America’s own GPS satellites, and could be used by its enemies.
 Now, however, the biggest gap is in satellite internet, where America has rocketed ahead. Europe’s closest answer to Starlink is OneWeb, whose parent company, Eutelsat, is partly owned by the French and British governments. (Britain bailed the firm out after it collapsed in 2020, and both countries injected more capital last year.) OneWeb was founded in 2012, three years before Starlink, but was rapidly eclipsed by it: as a division of SpaceX, Mr Musk’s world-beating rocket company, Starlink had plenty of cash to fuel its massive expansion (see chart). The entry of other private firms may widen America’s lead. Amazon’s Leo aims to offer satellite internet later this year.
 OneWeb has a number of terminals in Ukraine, some paid for by Germany, and is used by several European armed forces, including the French and British navies. It is also deployed on some aerial and naval drones. But it is not a direct replacement for Starlink. OneWeb has about 600 satellites; Starlink has more than 10,000. The European system cannot carry as much data or serve as many users in any one area. And because its satellites are in a much higher orbit, users need bigger terminals, the cheapest of which cost around $9,000—roughly 45 times more than a basic Starlink terminal. Kaja Kallas, the EU’s top diplomat, acknowledged this before meeting Mr Zelensky on October 16th: “Starlink is really necessary for Ukraine and unfortunately in the short term Europe can’t replace this capability.”
 The EU plans to spend €15bn ($17bn) on IRIS 2, a constellation of 348 communications satellites to be used by its members’ governments and armed forces. But the first will be launched only in 2029. Germany, meanwhile, plans its own network of 100 military-communications satellites at a cost of around €10bn. That has led to concerns of duplication and fragmentation.
 There is more encouraging news when it comes to the second area of concern, space-based ISR, mainly thanks to private European newcomers that produce small surveillance satellites much faster than legacy firms such as Airbus. Admiral Anders Sundeman, the head of Sweden’s space force, says that if asked a year ago how long it would take to launch his country’s first spy satellite, he would have estimated 2030. “We launched it instead this year,” he says (though the launch happened on an American Falcon 9 ride-share flight). It was made by Iceye, a Finnish startup that has figured out how to shrink radar satellites that were once as big as a car down to the size of a washing machine. Iceye has put 80 into orbit and plans to double its production rate to 100 next year. Sweden has also signed a deal to buy small spy satellites from Planet Labs, an American startup that recently opened a factory in Germany.
 Having lots of small, cheap satellites like these makes it easier to cope with losing a few to jamming, or to attack. That is a real risk. In mid-October a Russian satellite manoeuvred into a very close orbit with one made by Iceye that provides intelligence for Ukraine. Yet even if Ukraine’s satellite is disabled, the country has two more, along with access to intelligence from a number of European ones.
 Other American capabilities will take far longer to replace. One is a ballistic-missile warning system. France and Germany are teaming up to bui

docs.title: It looks like a music festival. It’s really a sales pitch for private credit.

Global 
 It looks like a music festival. It’s really a sales pitch for private credit.
 AnnaMaria Andriotis , The Wall Street Journal 13 min read 22 Oct 2026, 07:07 AM IST 
 Summary
 Fund managers are putting on elaborate events to court wealth advisers in hopes of reaching untapped household riches—even as some investors get spooked by risk. 
 Gift this article Check your portfolio 
 This is a Mint Premium article gifted to you.
Subscribe to enjoy similar stories.
 Subscribe now 
 Nearly 6,000 people descended last month on Huntington Beach, Calif., for musical performances by Wiz Khalifa and Gym Class Heroes, meditation and workout sessions, and classes on how to make whiskey-based cocktails, artisan pizza and sea-salt scrub.
 And, of course, to hear pitches on private credit and other investments.
 From afar, the four-day event, called the “Future Proof Festival,” looked like a rave. Up close, it was an example of the booming efforts to sell private-credit products to individual investors. Asset-management firms are targeting the largely untapped market as their traditional, large investors—endowments, pension funds and foundations—max out their desired exposure. Firms continue to pitch the products even as individuals are increasingly getting spooked by risks bubbling to the surface.
 Apollo Global Management and State Street held a session on private and public credit. Capital Group had a booth with a pickleball court and a session with a “Public-Private Solutions sales specialist” on the merging of private and public markets. Franklin Templeton talked about “building better portfolios” by adding private investments. Many attendees worked in the wealth-management industry—the gatekeeper to most individual investors.
 The festival also promoted a range of public investments, such as ETFs, and focused on technology used by wealth managers and other topics meant to support advisory businesses.
 Attendees, many in shorts, went on 15-minute “speed dating” sessions under a massive tent on the beach with fund managers and other companies that touted their offerings. The vibes put people at ease and helped evangelize private investments, attendees said.
 Melissa Joy came in part to learn about private credit and other private investments. The Dexter, Mich., investment adviser also took in a coastal photography class and a pub crawl. Her colleague, Alexa Kane, spent time at an adopt a puppy booth sponsored by Nuveen—last year she had snuggled the puppies and she went back to the booth this year.
 In recent years, private credit has ballooned from an opaque corner of the financial world into a multitrillion-dollar business. The sector undertakes financing that has traditionally been performed by banks—whether for lending to companies, private-equity deals or other transactions.
 Individual investors have flooded into funds that promise big gains by lending with relatively high interest rates to what would traditionally be considered risky companies. But the funds can be illiquid and charge high fees, and defaults in the past year have highlighted the investments’ risk.
 The firms behind the wave—including Apollo, Blackstone, Blue Owl, Carlyle and KKR, as well as much smaller shops—are aiming to get access to the household wealth of individual investors.
 In addition to the music and wellness festivals, events to pitch retail investors, financial advisers and family offices are happening at five-star hotels in Beverly Hills, Sonoma wine country retreats, holiday parties and steakhouse dinners. Ads have become ubiquitous around sports such as tennis and Formula One racing, touting “alternatives for investors” and options “empowering businesses.”
 Anthony Scaramucci’s flashy SALT hedge-fund conference is in talks to co-host events with Apex’s conference business, which holds private-capital gatherings that include fund managers and high-net-worth individuals, family offices and wealth managers, according to people familiar with the matter.
 Matt Middleton, the founder and CEO of Future Proof, said his company’s festival was mostly focused on topics related to running wealth-management firms such as technology, marketing, and client acquisition and retention and said private markets aren’t a big focus.
 Many say allowing individual investors access to the private-market funds levels the playing field and lets them earn the profits that large institutional investors have access to.
 Others say individuals are less capable of balancing the greater risks of private credit, including steep loan write-downs, fraud and fears about the impact of artificial-intelligence on private-credit-backed software companies.
 The poster child of the worries has been Blue Owl, which aggressively courted individuals. Early this year, concerns arose about its exposure to tech, including to companies at risk of being undercut by AI, and fears grew that it was in a liquidity crunch. Blue Owl offloaded $1.4 billion in loan assets at the beginning of the year, further worrying some investors and driving down its stock price. Investors have requested withdrawals of more than $10 billion from two of its funds this year.
 A Blue Owl spokesman said software remains one of its strongest performing segments and said liquidity has never been an issue. In early October, its flagship fund said more than 90% of its approximately 90,000 shareholders remained fully invested.
 More broadly, investors withdrew an estimated $30 billion from private-credit funds that are heavily marketed to individual investors in this year’s first three quarters, according to the latest data from investment bank Robert A. Stanger. And new retail money flowing in has slowed.

Near-term market outlook weak; DRL among 3 stock ideas: Ajit Mishra
 Stocks to buy today: The 22,200-22,400 zone is the next key support area, while the 23,000-23,300 zone is likely to cap the upside during any recovery.
 Illustration: Binay Sinha
 Ajit Mishra Mumbai 3 min read Last Updated : Oct 22 2026 | 7:48 AM IST
 Listen to This Article
 Disclaimer: This article is written by Ajit Mishra, SVP-research at Religare Broking. Views expressed are his own. Readers' discretion is advised. 
 Market View 
 Markets witnessed a sharp reversal on Wednesday, surrendering early gains amid profit booking and persistent macroeconomic concerns. The benchmark indices opened on a positive note, supported by strong buying in IT stocks and Reliance Industries, but selling pressure intensified as the session progressed. Consequently, the Nifty declined 0.88 per cent to close at 22,687.50, slipping below the 22,700 mark and highlighting the fragility of the recent recovery. 
 On the sectoral front, all sectors, barring IT, ended in the red, with metal, auto and energy emerging among the top laggards. Selling pressure was particularly severe in the broader market, where midcap and smallcap indices declined by around 1.5 per cent to 2.4 per cent, reflecting widespread risk aversion. 
 Global and domestic macroeconomic concerns continued to weigh on sentiment. Brent crude remained elevated around $110 per barrel amid escalating geopolitical tensions and concerns over potential supply disruptions. Although the rupee has strengthened recently, elevated oil prices, global bond yields and uncertainty surrounding foreign fund flows remain key risks. Meanwhile, the ongoing earnings season continues to drive stock-specific activity, with investors closely tracking corporate results and management commentary. 
 The selling pressure across key sectors, barring IT, has pushed the Nifty below its short-term moving average, the 20-day exponential moving average (20-DEMA), again weakening the near-term outlook. The 22,200–22,400 zone is the next key support area, while the 23,000–23,300 zone is likely to cap the upside during any recovery. Given elevated crude prices, weak broader-market participation and persistent geopolitical uncertainties, participants should maintain a cautious stance, focus on selective stock-specific opportunities and consider a balanced approach with appropriate positioning on both sides of the market.

The price action reflects stability, and a decisive move above 1,250 could further accelerate the upward momentum. One can consider accumulating the stock within the mentioned range.

Nifty can fall to 22500, says Jatin Gedia; shares 3 stock trading ideas
 The daily momentum indicator has a positive crossover; however, failure to hold the crucial support zone of 22850-22820 is a concern.
 Illustration: Binay Sinha
 Jatin Gedia Mumbai 2 min read Last Updated : Oct 22 2026 | 8:06 AM IST
 Listen to This Article
 Disclaimer: This article is written by Jatin Gedia - VP, Technical Research, Teji Mandi Investment Technologies. Views expressed are his own. Readers' discretion is advised. 
 Market outlook
 Nifty breached the rising channel support at 22850-22820 on the downside, turning the short-term trend negative again. Pullbacks towards 22900-22920 are likely to attract selling pressure. On the downside, the crucial support is now placed at the 22550-22500 zone, which coincides with the 61.8 per cent Fibonacci retracement level of the 22180-23175 rally. Brokerages bullish on Bajaj Finance despite margin and regulatory risks
 Bajaj Finance's Q2FY27 profit rose 29% to Rs 6,370 crore, with strong loan growth and higher AUM guidance supporting brokerage optimism despite regulatory and margin risks
 premium 
 BAF’s Q2FY27 profit after tax (PAT) grew 29 per cent year-on-year (YoY) to ₹6,370 crore, which was in line with consensus estimates
 Devangshu Datta New Delhi 4 min read Last Updated : Oct 21 2026 | 11:00 PM IST
 Listen to This Article
 Non-banking financial company Bajaj Finance reported strong performance in the September quarter (Q2FY27) with confident growth guidance despite headwinds like elevated oil prices, El Niño risks, a rising interest rate cycle and adverse regulatory changes. 
 Net interest margin (NIM) contracted slightly quarter-on-quarter (Q-o-Q). The company reported slippages in gold loans, which it termed transitory. Its investments in artificial intelligence (AI) and branch expansion are underway. A proposed equity capital raise of ₹17,500 crore, targeted for completion in Q3, will drive growth and return targets. 
 Bajaj Finance’s profit after tax (PAT) grew 29 per cent year-on-year (Y-o-Y) to ₹6,370 crore, in line with consensus estimates. Net interest income (NII), the difference between interest earned and interest expended, rose 24 per cent Y-o-Y, while non-interest income rose 11 per cent. Pre-provision operating profit rose 21 per cent Y-o-Y to ₹10,700 crore. Annualised credit costs remained stable Q-o-Q at 1.56 per cent after the firm added an overlay of ₹340 crore to provide for macroeconomic risks. Excluding this, credit costs fell 12 per cent Y-o-Y to around 1.32 per cent. Gross non-performing assets stood at 1.06 per cent, up 10 basis points (bps) Q-o-Q, while net NPAs rose 3 bps to 0.42 per cent. The provisioning coverage ratio on Stage 3 assets was stable sequentially at 60 per cent. Stage 2 and Stage 3 assets rose by ₹1,600 crore in Q2, including a ₹1,050 crore rise in Stage 2 gold loans. 
 The company expects full-year credit costs to remain close to the H1FY27 range. It has raised its FY27 assets under management (AUM) growth guidance to 26-27 per cent, while retaining its long-term growth guidance at 23-25 per cent. Growth momentum remains strong across segments, except MSMEs. 
 A key overhang is the Reserve Bank of India’s (RBI’s) proposed restrictions on revolving credit. A complete ban could affect AUM growth, NIM and profitability. Proposed changes to commissions could also weigh on fee income, prompting it to reassess its strategy. Medium-term fee income growth is likely to be in the 15-18 per cent range. 
 The company hopes the RBI will adopt a balanced approach to its proposed framework. It is also awaiting finalisation of the Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India’s (Irdai’s) proposed changes to insurance commissions and is evaluating scenarios. 
 The FinAI team has expanded to 328 employees, with 129 AI agents and 65 agentic applications. AI bots handle 75 per cent of do-it-yourself customer service volumes. Digital disbursements grew 111 per cent Y-o-Y. Early assessments of a customised business-to-business (B2B) risk model being tested across 500,000 accounts indicate the potential for a 15-20 per cent improvement in risk outcomes. The model could subsequently be extended to business-to-consumer (B2C) lending. 
 Total AUM grew to ₹5.85 trillion, with Q-o-Q growth led by gold loans (up 14 per cent), loan against securities (up 15 per cent), rural sales finance (up 7 per cent), consumer sales finance (up 6 per cent), micro­finance (up 8 per cent) and vehicle loans (up 6 per cent). MSME growth was lower at 3 per cent Q-o-Q, but it expects a rebound in H2. 
 Bajaj Finance acquired 4.4 million customers in Q2 and targets 60-62 million new loans and 18-20 million customer additions in FY27. NIM is expected to remain close to FY26 levels of 9.7 per cent. But the company said the contraction could exceed its initial guidance of 10-15 bps because of the rising interest rate cycle. It discontinued short-tenure gold loan schemes in August and said 55 per cent of the elevated Stage 2 balance had been resolved, with no material credit costs expected. Bajaj Finance is pruning its captive vehicle loan portfolio to reduce credit costs. Its gold loan AUM stands at ₹24,000 crore, which is 4 per cent of total AUM. 
 Strong loan growth and operating efficiencies should help offset margin pressures. Improving asset quality and a potential decline in credit costs could accelerate profit growth. The stronger growth guidance may also prompt brokerages to raise earnings estimates. PAT could grow at close to 30 per cent annually through FY28, with management guiding for a return on equity (RoE) of 19-21 per cent in FY28. Though macroeconomic headwinds and regulatory changes remain key risks, Bajaj Finance is better placed than most peers to weather the situation. 
 According to Bloomberg, 24 of the 32 analysts polled in October were bullish on the stock, while four each were bearish or neutral. Their one-year target price was ₹1,175, compared with Wednesday’s BSE closing price of ₹925.10.
 The writer is New Delhi-based independent journalist

docs.title: 3 ‘Buy’ recommendations by Jefferies with 21% to 32% upside
docs.text: Jefferies retained its ‘Buy’ rating on UltraTech Cement and Bajaj Finance in reports dated October 20, 2026, while keeping a ‘Buy’ on Hindustan Zinc with a lower target price. The brokerage’s October 20 information technology report also identified buying opportunities among select mid-sized IT companies, including Sagility India. UltraTech Cement: ‘Buy’ Jefferies reiterated its ‘Buy’ rating on UltraTech Cement and raised its target price to Rs 14,380 from Rs 14,065. The brokerage said cement pricing would be a key factor in sustaining earnings improvement as costs rise. UltraTech reported year-on-year growth of 14% in domestic cement demand in the September quarter, ahead of industry demand growth of about 10%. Its blended earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA) per tonne came in at Rs 975, above Jefferies’ estimate of around Rs 900. The brokerage noted that cement prices strengthened from mid-September and that October spot prices were about 5% above September-quarter levels. Management remained committed to an EBITDA-per-tonne target of Rs 1,400 by the exit of the March 2028 quarter. Bajaj Finance: ‘Buy’ Jefferies maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on Bajaj Finance but lowered its target price to Rs 1,230 from Rs 1,280 after trimming its estimates for the following financial years. The company’s assets under management grew 26% year on year in the September quarter, compared with 24% in the June quarter. Net interest income rose 24%, while fee income increased 33%. The brokerage said a rise in stage-2 loans in the gold-loan segment needed monitoring, but management expected the profit-and-loss impact to be negligible. Jefferies also identified regulatory decisions on flexi-loans and bancassurance fees as areas to watch. Its estimates factor in some impact from potential restrictions, partly offset by stronger loan growth. Hindustan Zinc: ‘Buy’ Jefferies retained its ‘Buy’ rating on Hindustan Zinc but cut its target price to Rs 650 from Rs 750, citing lower assumptions for silver prices. The company’s September-quarter EBITDA rose 15% sequentially and came in 8% above Jefferies’ estimate. Lower production costs and higher lead concentrate sales supported the result. The brokerage said zinc prices had benefited from tight supply conditions, including mine closures, lower ore grades and project delays. Silver prices, however, had been volatile since June 2026, while rising interest rates could add near-term pressure. Jefferies said a recovery in silver prices would be important for the stock’s performance. Sagility India: ‘Buy’ Jefferies identified Sagility as a mid-sized IT company with rerating potential in its October 20 report on the sector. The brokerage said the company stood out among mid-sized IT stocks on its assessment of potential valuation upside and downside risk. With a target price of Rs 54% indicating an upside of around 23%. The report said market valuations were pricing in lower long-term revenue growth than companies had delivered historically. Jefferies also cautioned that the broader IT sector’s growth outlook remained muted, making stock selection important. docs.title: Why Motilal Oswal is bullish on this realty stock despite a 54% profit fall
docs.text: The domestic brokerage house Motilal Oswal has kept its 'Buy' rating on real estate stock and set a target price of Rs 1,710 per share. That is about 45% above the stock’s current market price. The call follows the company’s results for the Q2FY27, the three months from July to September 2026. According to the brokerage report, the Bengaluru-based developer, Sobha, posted its highest-ever quarterly collections from homebuyers and kept its sales growth target for the year. But the same results show revenue down 31% and profit down by more than half. Why is the brokerage still bullish? Here is what the report says. Sobha has more projects in the pipeline. For property developers, launching a project is only the first step. The real test is how quickly buyers book homes and how much money the company collects from those sales. ALSO READRevenue up 200%, profit up 88%: Is this logistics smallcap just getting started? Sobha’s pre-sales rose 16% year-on-year to Rs 2,210 crore in the September quarter of FY27. This was its second-highest quarterly booking figure. Bengaluru remained its largest market, accounting for 60% of bookings, followed by the National Capital Region (NCR) at 27%. The next few quarters could bring more opportunities. According to Motilal Oswal’s report, Sobha has 18 projects in its upcoming launch pipeline, covering 20.4 million square feet and carrying a combined gross development value (GDV) of Rs 31,400 crore. Eight of these projects, valued at around Rs 18,000 crore, are expected to launch in the second half of FY27. That gives Sobha a sizeable opportunity to bring more homes to market. The company is targeting 30% year-on-year growth in pre-sales for FY27, equivalent to around Rs 10,500 crore in bookings. Motilal Oswal estimates that pre-sales could reach Rs 13,000 crore by FY28. More bookings are coming in, but is enough cash being generated? Sobha’s residential collections increased 4% year-on-year to Rs 1,920 crore in the September quarter, its highest-ever quarterly figure. Motilal Oswal expects residential collections to grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 21% between FY26 and FY28, reaching Rs 10,300 crore. However. net operational cash flow declined 14% year-on-year to Rs 440 crore, while land investment spending increased 76% to Rs 620 crore during the quarter. ALSO READBajaj Finance share price falls 3%; Brokerages see 26-34% upside on growth across segments Can sales growth translate into profits? Despite higher bookings, the company’s revenue fell 31% year-on-year to Rs 970 crore in the September quarter. EBITDA declined 28% to Rs 68.7 crore, while adjusted profit after tax (PAT) dropped 54.6% to Rs 33 crore. Motilal Oswal has valued Sobha’s ongoing and upcoming projects at Rs 14,800 crore using a discounted cash flow (DCF) method. It has not assigned value to an additional 1,745 acres of land that remain under various stages of consolidation. docs.title: UltraTech Cement share price up 3%: Jefferies sees 34% upside on C&W bet
docs.text: The UltraTech Cement share price soared nearly 3% today, October 21. The country’s largest cement major posted robust numbers for the second quarter of financial year 2027 (Q2FY27). Cost pressures stemming from the West Asia war are likely to remain in the near term, with some analysts expecting price hikes to offset the input cost increase. Global investment bank Jefferies has a ‘Buy’ rating on the stock, and it also raised the price target by over 2% to Rs 14,380 apiece. This implies an upside of nearly 34% from the stock’s current price of Rs 10,735. Japanese brokerage Nomura maintained its ‘Buy’ recommendation on the stock, but lowered the target price by over 1% to Rs 13,700. This implies an upside of around 28%. Domestic brokerage Motilal Oswal also maintained its ‘Buy’ call on UltraTech, and has a target price of Rs 13,220, reflecting an upside of 23% from the current price. ALSO READ57x growth in solar capacity: 2 stocks betting big on India’s next solar wave UltraTech Q2 earnings UltraTech Cement reported a 21% year-on-year (YoY) increase in net profit for the second quarter of financial year 2027 (Q2FY27), driven by higher sales volumes and improved operating performance. Its net profit rose to Rs 1,494 crore from Rs 1,232 crore a year ago. However, the bottom line fell short of the Bloomberg consensus estimate of Rs 1,604 crore. UltraTech’s revenue for the September quarter rose nearly 19% YoY to Rs 23,295 crore, beating the Bloomberg estimate of Rs 22,342 crore. Jefferies on UltraTech: C&W biz to scale beyond expectations Jefferies reiterated UltraTech as its top pick in the sector, with a sustained recovery in cement price remaining the key catalyst for the stock. It has a ‘Buy’ rating on the stock, with a price target of Rs 14,380 apiece, implying an upside of nearly 34%. Jefferies noted that the company’s management discussed extensively on cement prices rather than volumes. It highlighted that pricing momentum has improved since mid September and that the company will focus on protecting EBITDA per tonne despite higher costs. The company also raised expectations for its cables and wires (C&W) business. UltraTech expects the C&W business to scale ahead of initial expectations, with the current expansion supporting a revised revenue target of Rs 1,600 crore to Rs 1,800 crore, from Rs 1,000 crore earlier. This is mostly driven by higher copper prices. “Pricing remains market-aligned, with select products commanding a premium. Mgmt clarified no entry into fans and other electricals and expects FY28 to be the first meaningful year of scale for the business,” Jefferies said. Nomura on UltraTech: Lower EBITDA view Nomura has lowered its EBITDA estimates for FY27 by 5% to Rs 18,200 crore. It has also reduced its FY28 and FY29 EBITDA projections by 1% each to Rs 23,000 crore and Rs 25,500 crore, respectively. This is largely on account of the escalated cost structure. Nomura maintained its ‘Buy’ recommendation on the stock, with a target price of Rs 13,700, implying an upside of around 28%. Higher fuel costs remain a concern but Nomura expects price hikes to offset the spot fuel costs. “Management expects demand to stay strong through March 2029E, supported by data centers, private capex, metro extensions and urban housing, although a weaker monsoon typically leads to softer rural demand, which could pose a risk in FY28F, in our view,” Nomura said. Motilal Oswal on UltraTech: Extending lead over peers Motilal Oswal also maintained its ‘Buy’ call on UltraTech, and has a target price of Rs 13,220, reflecting an upside of 23% from the current price. ALSO READIndian IT stocks rally 12% in a week – Is the turnaround sustainable? “The company reported robust volume growth and witnessed strong improvement in capacity utilisation. Cement prices have recovered since Sep’26 and seen improvement in early-Oct’26. However, cost pressure remains a key near-term challenge. UTCEM continues to extend its lead over peers across capacity, market share, cost leadership, and cash flow generation,” the brokerage said. Motilal Oswal expects the company’s consolidated revenue to rise 13% on a compounded annual growth rate (CAGR) basis over FY26 to FY28. It expects EBITDA to grow 14% CAGR and net profit at 15% CAGR over the same period. docs.title: Bajaj Finance share price falls 3%; Brokerages see 26-34% upside on growth across segments
docs.text: The Bajaj Finance share price slumped nearly 3% in early trade today, October 21. The shares are in focus after the company reported its earnings for the second quarter of financial year 2027 (Q2FY27) on Monday, October 19. Global investment bank Jefferies maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on the stock, with a price target of Rs 1,230 apiece. This implies an upside of over 31% from the stock’s current price of Rs 936.15 apiece. Jefferies said Bajaj Finance is amongst its top picks in the sector. Domestic brokerages Motilal Oswal and Nuvama have maintained their ‘Buy’ ratings on the stock. Motilal Oswal has a target price of Rs 1,250 for Bajaj Finance, implying an upside of 34% from the stock’s current price of Rs 936.15 apiece. Nuvama has a price target of Rs 1,175, implying an upside of around 26%. ALSO READ57x growth in solar capacity: 2 stocks betting big on India’s next solar wave Bajaj Finance Q2 earnings Bajaj Finance on Monday reported a 29% year-on-year rise in consolidated profit after tax to Rs 6,367 crore for the September quarter, as its lending business expanded and net interest income increased. The figure is before minority interest, according to the company’s investor presentation released on October 19. Assets under management rose 26% to Rs 5,84,624 crore as of September 30, 2026, from Rs 4,62,261 crore a year earlier. Profit before tax increased 29% to Rs 8,537 crore. Jefferies on Bajaj Finance: Amongst the top picks in the sector Strong growth in assets under management (AUM) led the growth in top line for the quarter. “Stressed loans saw a slight rise from gold loans, but mgt sees a negligible P&L impact & confirmed that AQ stays strong. Clarity on flexi-loans & banca fees will be watched & mgt is taking mitigating steps,” Jefferies said. Bajaj Finance continues to be a strong platform, and Jefferies retained it amongst the top picks for the sector. Jefferies said the two regulatory issues that will be monitorable are RBI's final directions on flexi-loans and IRDAI's direction on bancassurance fees. “Even as management is hopeful that regulators will take a balanced approach, they are working to mitigate product risks. We factor a 35% fall in bancassurance fees, and partly lower yields to consider some impact of restrictions on flexi-loans,” it said. Motilal Oswal on Bajaj Finance: Sustainable earnings compounding phase Brokerage Motilal Oswal believes Bajaj Finance is entering a phase of sustainable earnings compounding, driven by broad-based growth, resilient profitability, and improving asset quality. The company’s management remains optimistic about the FY27 credit cost outlook and expects the full-year credit cost to remain within the H1FY27 range. This will be supported by improving portfolio performance, proactive underwriting, and prudent overlays. Motilal Oswal sees credit costs of 1.5% each in FY27 and FY28. The brokerage has raised its FY27 and FY28 estimated earnings per share (EPS) view by 1% and 4%, respectively. This factors in stronger growth in assets under management and benefit on net interest margins (NIMs) from the proposed equity capital raising of Rs 17,500 crore, which Motilal expects to be completed by December. “Bajaj Finance delivered a healthy quarter, with broad-based growth across segments and continued improvement in asset quality, supported by strong vintage performance and stable credit costs. While there was some marginal asset quality deterioration, largely driven by gold loans, management remains confident of negligible ultimate credit losses. Margins declined during the quarter and could witness further (organic) contraction due to expected rise in borrowing costs,” the brokerage said. Motilal Oswal on Bajaj Finance: Key risks The brokerage said any potential asset quality deterioration due to weak monsoon, El Nino, and higher crude oil price pose risk to the company’s growth outlook. If the RBI’s proposed restrictions on revolving credit are implemented in their current form, Bajaj Finance could see an impact on its AUM growth and pressure on NIMs. Lower fee income due to the proposed IRDAI regulations on insurance commissions also pose a risk. ALSO READIndian IT stocks rally 12% in a week – Is the turnaround sustainable? Nuvama on Bajaj Finance: Diversified portfolio to sustain growth Nuvama has maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on the stock and has a target price of Rs 1,175, implying an upside of 34%. It believes accelerating growth and contained credit costs shall help Bajaj Finance sustain healthy return on assets, returns on AUM, and returns on equity. Nuvama says the company’s diversified portfolio and proactive risk management position it well to sustain healthy growth and manage asset quality despite emerging macroeconomic headwinds. “Management expects the AUM growth momentum to continue in FY27E (26–27%) while retaining medium-term growth guidance of 23–25% despite planned heavy capital raise. However, they expect margins to contract 10–15bp in FY27E due to repo rate hike, but better operational efficiency and credit cost should support its otherwise strong RoAuM. Management believes the regulatory impact of insurance commission capping and revolver loan is manageable and should not hurt their medium-term RoAuM guidance around 4.3–4.7%,” Nuvama said. docs.title: Nomura initiates coverage on two renewable players with up to 26% upside
docs.text: India has one of the largest installed renewable capacities in the world. With the share of renewable energy increasing in the country’s electricity mix, issues such as grid instability and mismatch in the timing of power generation and consumption are popping up. Japanese brokerage Nomura has initiated coverage on two renewable players, ACME Solar Holdings and NTPC Green Energy, as it expects these companies to benefit from the rising use of renewable energy. Nomura has initiated coverage with a ‘Buy’ rating on ACME Solar and has a target price of Rs 505. This implies an upside of 26% from the stock’s current price of Rs 400.15 apiece. For NTPC Green, the brokerage has a ‘Neutral’ rating and a target price of Rs 100. This reflects an upside of nearly 19% from its current price of Rs 84.14 apiece. ALSO READ57x growth in solar capacity: 2 stocks betting big on India’s next solar wave Nomura on ACME Solar Nomura expects ACME Solar to add 4.3 gigawatt (GW) of contracted capacities over FY27 to FY29. This will drive a revenue growth of 66% on a compounded annual growth rate (CAGR) basis and earnings before interest, tax, depreciation, and amortisation (EBITDA) growth of 65% CAGR over the same period. The company is transitioning from a conventional solar independent power producer into a firm, dispatchable platform, with firm and dispatchable renewable energy (FDRE) now forming more than half of its total portfolio capacity. FDRE projects are structured around pairing larger generation assets with storage, enabling developers to match a utility's defined delivery schedule and consumption pattern, Nomura said. ACME Solar has been able to expand margins following the decline in Lithium-ion cell prices over the past few years, and projects won at tariffs assuming higher battery energy storage system (BESS) cost. The company is benefitting from margin improvement for a second time through early commissioning of BESS. “By installing BESS at sites where solar is already operational, it reuses existing evacuation infrastructure and energizes the battery into the merchant market ahead of FDRE CoD, with over 5 GWh already operating this way. Pulling BESS online one year early adds more than 1,000bp to project equity IRR, we estimate,” the brokerage said. ACME Solar’s strong order pipeline provides earnings growth visibility through FY29, subject to its commissioning schedules. ACME’s total portfolio is around 8.1 GW as of June 2026, which rose to 8.4 GW on a recent 300 MW FDRE award. Only about 3 GW is operational currently, with the under-construction book carrying signed power purchase agreements on roughly 4.3 GW of storage-linked capacity and a further 1.1 GW awaiting signature. Nomura on NTPC Green NTPC Green Energy is the renewable subsidiary of state-owned NTPC. Nomura expects the company’s revenue to expand at 74% CAGR over FY27 to FY29 and EBITDA to rise 72% CAGR over the same period. This will be driven by consolidated capacity additions of 18 GW over the same period. NTPC has committed to 60 GW of renewable capacity by FY32, with NTPC Green Energy as the group's principal renewable vehicle. NTPC Green has around 12.9GW of under-construction capacity in its wholly owned subsidiary and 3.4GW under joint ventures, with the balance to be built out through further tender wins. ALSO READUltraTech Cement share price up 3%: Jefferies sees 34% upside on C&W bet “This materially reduces pipeline replenishment risk, which we regard as the principal constraint on growth for Indian renewable developers; MoUs carry a second-order benefit: they give NGEL access to land parcels and state transmission connectivity, easing the two conditions that most commonly delay commissioning, in our view,” Nomura said. “As an NTPC subsidiary, NGEL inherits both execution capability and relatively low funding cost. The parent's track record across large projects provides NGEL with a delivery capability that is difficult to replicate, in our view. The sharper advantage is relatively low cost of debt. The benefit further adds up with cheaper debt supporting higher leverage at the same coverage ratio, so less equity is locked into each megawatt, and the same equity base rotates through more projects,” Nomura added. docs.title: Yes Bank shares plunge 21% in 5 days: Nomura cuts target to Rs 18 after AT1 verdict
docs.text: Yes Bank shares have come under pressure, falling more than 21% in the past five trading sessions and around 23% so far in 2026. The latest concern is not just about the bank’s quarterly earnings, but also the financial impact of a Supreme Court ruling on its additional tier-1 (AT1) bonds. Global brokerage Nomura has maintained its ‘Neutral’ rating on Yes Bank but lowered its target price to Rs 18 from Rs 23. The new target implies an upside of around 6.5% from the stock’s current market price at the time of the report. According to the brokerage report, the ruling could affect the bank’s capital position and reported earnings, even as its September-quarter profit broadly matched expectations. Here are the key factors investors need to watch - Why has the AT1 bond verdict become a concern? The Supreme Court’s ruling to restore Yes Bank’s previously written-down AT1 bonds worth Rs 8,415 crore has emerged as a key concern for investors. ALSO READ5 budget-friendly stocks under Rs 50 to track According to Nomura, restoring these bonds could have a post-tax profit and loss impact of around Rs 6,300 crore. That is approximately 1.8 times the bank’s net profit in FY26. The brokerage estimates that the bank’s common equity tier-1 (CET1) capital ratio could also decline by around 230 basis points from its current level of 13.7%. The potential impact is significant because CET1 capital acts as a financial cushion against unexpected losses. Nomura noted that the ruling “might impact P&L by ~Rs 6,300 crore (1.8x FY26 PAT) and reduce the bank's CET1 ratio by approximately 230bp”. Yes Bank’s Q2 results: Why did profit beat estimates? The bank reported profit before tax (PBT) of Rs 1,360 crore for the Q2FY27, up 4% sequentially. Net interest income (NII) came in at Rs 2,820 crore, slightly ahead of Nomura’s estimate. However, the underlying performance was mixed. Higher operating expenses and lower fee income weighed on the bank’s core pre-provision operating profit (PPOP). As per the brokerage report, better treasury income and a lower tax rate helped offset these pressures. The bank’s net profit after tax (PAT) was 6% above Nomura’s estimate. ALSO READYES Bank sees 250 bps hit on AT1 revival The brokerage also highlighted that the net interest margin (NIM) declined by 10 basis points sequentially to 2.69%. It attributed most of the decline to foreign currency non-resident bank (FCNR(B)) deposits. Loan growth improves, but what about the outlook? Yes Bank’s overall loan growth stood at 18% year-on-year. Corporate banking loans grew 30%, while commercial banking loans increased 20%. Retail loan growth improved to 9% from 7% in the previous quarter, although it remained comparatively slower. However, Nomura has reduced its earnings estimates for FY27 and FY28 by 2% to 13%, after accounting for higher operating expenses and normalising credit costs. What is Nomura’s target for Yes Bank? Nomura has cut its target price to Rs 18 from Rs 23 and retained its ‘Neutral’ rating. The brokerage has also lowered the valuation multiple it applies to the bank, reflecting the uncertainty surrounding the AT1 bond ruling. docs.title: 57x growth in solar capacity: 2 stocks betting big on India’s next solar wave
docs.text: India’s solar energy sector is entering a new phase of growth. Installed solar capacity has increased from less than 3 gigawatts (GW) in 2014 to around 171 GW in 2026, driven by rising electricity demand amid a shift towards renewable energy. The pace of expansion is also picking up. India added around 34 GW of solar capacity in the first half of 2026, up 38% year-on-year, while full-year additions are projected to reach nearly 50 GW. This growth brings opportunities across the solar value chain. Domestic manufacturing is expanding as companies invest in solar modules, cells, and upstream production facilities. At the same time, the rising number of utility-scale solar projects is creating demand for engineering, procurement, construction, and renewable energy asset management services. Upstream Integration vs. Turnkey EPC: Structural Comparison Against this backdrop, this article looks at two distinct business models that offer an interesting perspective on India’s solar growth story. One is strengthening its position through domestic solar manufacturing, capacity expansion, and backward integration, while the other is building its business around renewable energy project execution and a growing international footprint. docs.title: ‘Centre weighing Rs 35,000-cr outlay for PM-KUSUM-II’: MNRE’s Santosh Kumar Sarangi
docs.text: The government is considering an outlay of around Rs 35,000 crore for a follow-up to PM-KUSUM, broadly in line with the existing scheme, while seeking to link farm solarisation more closely with efficient irrigation and water conservation, MNRE Secretary Santosh Kumar Sarangi told FE. He also explained how the government seeks to resolve a tapering demand for "vanilla" solar projects, and why "acceptable prices" are important to attract buyers. Edited excerpts: Q. What is being planned after PM-KUSUM? Could the new programme have an outlay similar to the existing scheme? ALSO READRs 1.86 lakh cr grid push: 2 ‘under-the-radar’ transformer stocks with 40%+ ROCE A. The financial support could be broadly similar to the existing PM-KUSUM outlay, though the final amount has not been decided. The next phase is being discussed with the Agriculture Ministry with a greater focus on convergence between renewable energy and agriculture. It could incorporate modern water-conservation measures and more effective irrigation planning, rather than treating solar pumps as a standalone intervention. The structure and funding mechanism are still under discussion. The existing PM-KUSUM programme has central financial support of about Rs 34,422 crore. In several cases work is going on in the current scheme but payments have not been made. So there may be some spillover (in case of funds). In the case of legacy schemes, any legacy amount usually gets carried forward. Q. A large renewable project pipeline is facing delays in signing PPAs and PSAs. A. Some developers might exit as demand for plain, or “vanilla”, solar projects (those without backward integration/storage support etc.) has weakened. Recent regulatory changes have provided an exit route without the earlier consequence of forfeiting certain bank guarantees linked to connectivity. Some people will exit because the interest in vanilla solar is not very high. But vanilla solar with BESS is now selling well. Rather than simply replacing every surrendered project with an identical tender, SECI is being asked to first understand what states and distribution companies actually require. What we have now pushed SECI to do is to constantly talk to the states and discoms, understand their power profile and requirements, and only after understanding bring out those bids. The idea was you keep on tendering, people will eventually buy. But we have reached a point where people are not going to buy vanilla solar. You have to offer them in a configuration that will be acceptable to them, and not only configuration but also the prices that are acceptable. Q. Can India sustain renewable additions of around 50 GW annually? A. This will be sustainable provided we also pick up on battery manufacturing capacity. Dependence on imported batteries currently creates long delivery periods. Domestic manufacturing could accelerate storage deployment substantially. CEA projections envisage another 400 GW of renewable capacity by 2035–36, requiring battery storage, pumped hydro and green hydrogen to support growing solar and wind generation. Q. Where does PM Surya Ghar stand against its one-crore household target? A. Around 60 lakh households have been covered so far, with installations expected to cross 85 lakh and potentially reach 90 lakh by March 2027. ALSO READ2 Electrolyser stocks in India’s Rs 19,744-cr green hydrogen race—Who has the edge? It has picked up pace, so we are confident of touching 85 to 90 [lakh]. The remaining roughly 10 lakh could take “one or two months” beyond March. Q. Why has offshore wind failed to attract the same investor interest as solar and onshore wind? A. Economics remain difficult. Onshore wind costs about Rs 7-7.5 crore/MW, against roughly Rs 25 crore/MW for offshore wind. Offshore power could cost around Rs 8-9/unit, while solar is available at Rs 2.40-2.50. In India's case, the choice today is not compelling in favour of offshore wind because you have alternative access to cheaper electricity. The ministry is examining ways to attract developers without committing substantially higher incentives.

docs.title: 4x oil production target by FY30: An under-the-radar smallcap betting on bigger profits
docs.text: For years, Asian Energy Services made money by helping other companies look for oil and gas. It provided the technical services needed to understand what lay beneath the ground, develop fields and keep energy infrastructure running. It did not need to own the oil to earn from the business. Now, it wants a bigger share of the economics. The company is expanding from technical services into oil and gas production, adding an international services business and building out its mineral infrastructure operations. The attraction is straightforward. A company that provides services, earns fees for the work it performs. But a company that owns a producing oilfield can also benefit from the hydrocarbons it extracts. FE Stock Insights on WhatsApPGet instant alerts on high-conviction investment themes and fundamental deep dives—direct from Financial Express.Join now Asian Energy Services 1-Year Share Price Chart Source: Screener.in That second business comes with a different set of risks. Producing oil requires capital, output can disappoint and commodity prices can change the economics of a project. The question is whether Asian Energy Services can turn this shift into a more profitable business, rather than simply a larger one. From finding oil to producing it Asian Energy Services has more than three decades of experience in specialist services such as seismic surveys. These surveys help energy companies understand what lies beneath the ground before deciding where to drill. The company later expanded into engineering, procurement and construction (EPC), operations and maintenance (O&M), integrated field development and mineral infrastructure. The next step came in September 2025, when Asian Energy Services moved forward with the proposed merger of Oilmax Energy. The National Company Law Tribunal sanctioned the merger on 29 September 2026 and the company received the certified order on 15 October 2026. The merger brings producing and developing oil and gas assets into the business, extending its role from providing services to energy companies to earning directly from oil production. It brings producing and developing oil and gas assets into the group, moving Asian Energy Services beyond simply earning fees for providing services. It can now also benefit from the oil and gas produced from these assets. ALSO READ4 Small-Cap Stocks with Rising Promoter Stakes for Two Consecutive Quarters The businesses could complement one another. Seismic surveys help identify resources, field development prepares them for production and maintenance keeps facilities running. Oilmax adds the opportunity to earn from the hydrocarbons themselves, while mineral infrastructure provides a separate source of business linked to mining and material handling. More importantly, Oilmax could change the economics of the company. Oil production can generate higher margins and faster cash flows than project-based services. If production increases as planned, it could lift the group’s profitability and reduce its dependence on the services business. But that benefit is not automatic. Developing oilfields requires capital and production can fall short of expectations. The real test is whether Asian Energy Services can turn its broader business into higher margins, stronger cash flows and better returns for shareholders. Revenue has taken off. Margins have gone the other way The recent numbers show that the expansion is changing the company’s growth. Consolidated revenue from operations rose 70.1% in FY26. EBITDA grew at roughly half the rate of sales and the EBITDA margin fell from approximately 15.6% to 12.5%. In other words, the company generated substantially more revenue but retained a smaller share of each rupee as operating earnings. Kuiper, an international energy-services business, was acquired in 2025 and has been included in Asian Energy Services’ consolidated results since September that year. Some of the reported growth reflects adding a business that was not included in the previous year’s full-year consolidated figures. The company also reported an exceptional charge of Rs 9.4 crore in FY26, including acquisition-related costs and a write-off. Reported profit and profit adjusted for exceptional items should therefore be kept separate when assessing its performance. The June quarter of FY27 showed faster growth, but the margin question remained. Consolidated revenue increased 135% year on year. Yet the EBITDA margin declined to 8.1% from 10.5% in the corresponding quarter a year earlier. The company has cited the volatile Middle East operating environment, while the mix of contracts also influences quarterly margins. These factors may explain part of the pressure, but investors need to see the improvement in profitability in the reported numbers. Faster revenue growth is useful only if more of that revenue eventually reaches the bottom line and generates cash. Why the Rs 1,754 Crore Order Book is Only Half the Story The standalone order book stands at about Rs 1,754 crore. Oil and gas services account for 60%, with mineral services making up the rest. The figure excludes Kuiper and Oilmax, as well as covering third-party contracts for the standalone business. Asian Energy Services’ Rs 1,754 Crore Order Book: Where the Business Stands Source: Company Presentation Management has also identified an active bidding pipeline of Rs 3,000 crore to Rs 4,000 crore. These are opportunities, not confirmed orders. Winning them is one thing; delivering them at profitable margins is another. The order book, therefore, tells only part of the story. Projects can be delayed, costs can rise and customer payments can take time. Growth creates value only when the company earns a reasonable return on the work it undertakes. docs.title: Beyond Titan and Kalyan: The smallcaps supplying India’s jewellery giants
docs.text: India’s B2B jewellery manufacturers are catching market attention. Sky Gold has surged around 200% in 2026 so far. Meanwhile, other B2B jewellery manufacturers have also seen sharp gains. Shringar House of Mangalsutra rose nearly 50% in October till date, while Shanti Gold gained 109.5% in 2026 so far. The trend points to growing interest in companies that manufacture jewellery for retail chains rather than sell directly to consumers. The difference lies in the business model. B2C jewellers like Titan Company and Kalyan Jewellers need showrooms, retail staff and marketing to reach customers. B2B manufacturers, on the other hand, can grow by supplying multiple jewellery retailers. They can focus on production, design and order execution without having to build an extensive retail network. The timing also matters. Organised jewellers are projected to increase their share of India’s jewellery market from 35.2% in CY23 to 59.7% by CY29. As these retailers open more stores and refresh their collections, their need for reliable manufacturing partners could rise. FE Stock Insights on WhatsApPGet instant alerts on high-conviction investment themes and fundamental deep dives—direct from Financial Express.Join now For B2B jewellery manufacturers, this offers an opportunity to benefit from the expansion of organised retail without bearing the full cost of running consumer-facing stores. Against this backdrop, let’s look at three lesser-known small-cap jewellery companies that could benefit from this shift. #1 Shanti Gold: Doubling Capacity to Feed India's Mega-Retailers Shanti Gold International (market cap: ₹3,000 crore) is an Indian B2B gold jewellery manufacturer serving large organised retail chains, regional retailers, and international markets. It specialises in Cubic Zirconia (CZ) casting and studded gold jewellery (70-75% of its product sales mix) and plain gold jewellery (25-30%). Order-Book Expansion: Tapping North India and High-Margin Turkish Designs The company is now expanding into high-volume machine-made plain gold jewellery and value-added categories such as Turkish and designer jewellery. Shanti Gold serves major national and regional brands including Kalyan Jewellers, Joyalukkas, Lalithaa Jewellery and Bhima Jewellers. Shanti Gold has an installed capacity of 6,700 kg per annum after commissioning an additional 4,000 kg per annum. The company is adding another 1,200 kg of annual capacity, bringing total capacity to 7,900 kg per annum once the Jaipur facility becomes operational. The company expects to bring this capacity online by December 2026. It is scaling value-added sub-categories such as Turkish jewellery and introducing high-volume machine-made plain gold jewellery. Management is also expanding into North Indian markets where it does not yet have access. Shanti Gold delivered strong Q1FY27 performance. Sales volume reached 522.1 kg, up 61.6% year-on-year from 323.0 kg in Q1 FY26. Deeper engagement with existing organised retail clients, the rollout of new designs and entry into new domestic markets such as Northern India supported growth. As a result, revenue from operations jumped 144.7% to ₹716.38 crore. Net profit doubled to ₹50 crore. Guidance vs Delivery: Can 30-40% Volume Run-Rate Sustain 8% EBITDA Margins? Looking ahead, the management estimates revenue of ₹3,500 crore in FY27, comprising 50-60% value growth and 30-40% volume growth. Management expects the 30-40% volume growth trajectory to be sustainable over the next 3 to 4 years. Management expects sustainable EBITDA margins to settle in the 7.5-8.0% range. docs.title: Yes Bank Faces AT1 Bond Blow: Morgan Stanley Retains ‘Underweight’
docs.text: Morgan Stanley has called the Supreme Court’s decision upholding the quashing of Yes Bank’s additional tier-1 (AT1) bond write-off a negative for the lender, with the final impact hinging on how the ruling is interpreted and implemented. The investment bank said the key issue is whether the decision challenges the loss-absorption feature of AT1 bonds or relates to the procedure followed during the bank’s 2020 reconstruction. Morgan Stanley retained its ‘Underweight’ rating on YES Bank and a price target of Rs 17 in its October 15 research update. The Supreme Court upheld a January 2023 Bombay High Court order that quashed the bank’s write-off of AT1 bonds. “The post tax amount of ~Rs63bn implies ~12% of net worth and shaves off ~190bp of Yes bank's current CET I of ~14%,” Morgan Stanley said. The ruling raises questions about AT1 bond loss absorption The bank wrote off Rs 8,410 crore of AT1 bonds in March 2020. Morgan Stanley said it is waiting for details on the proportion of those bonds that will ultimately be allowed to remain written off. The final outcome could affect the bank’s capital position, but the investment bank’s broader concern is the legal basis for the decision. “A detail that we will be looking for in the decision is whether the loss absorption feature of ATI bonds has been fundamentally challenged or does the decision have more to do with the process followed by the administrator (of Yes Bank's 2020 reconstruction scheme),” Morgan Stanley said. ALSO READFrom Samosa oil to jet fuel: 7 Indian stocks set to benefit from SAF The distinction is important to how the ruling may be understood beyond Yes Bank itself. The investment bank is also watching for any review petition or clarification from the bank following the court order. Morgan Stanley awaits the bank’s next move Morgan Stanley noted that the legal uncertainty had weighed on the stock and that Yes Bank had reacted sharply to the news. The investment bank said it would watch for a possible review petition and for clarification from the lender on the implications of the ruling. ALSO READTonbo Imaging India IPO allotment: How to check status on BSE, NSE, KFin Technologies The firm’s cautious stance also reflects risks beyond the bond dispute, including weaker-than-expected loan and deposit growth, greater competition and a possible deterioration in asset quality. On the upside, Morgan Stanley identified lower macroeconomic risks and stronger growth in higher-margin lending as factors that could improve the outlook. docs.title: Intense selling on higher levels as Nifty, Sensex fail to hold gains
docs.text: A day of wild swings for the Indian equity market. After opening higher on Wednesday, October 21, the benchmark indices slipped sharply by the afternoon, but then pared some of these losses to close slightly lower. The Nifty 50 ended at 22,811.35 points, down 77.60 points, or 0.3%. The Sensex closed at 73.709.69 points, down 143.21 points, or 0.2% lower. The day’s lows During the day, the Nifty slipped to a low of 22,649.90 points, 1% lower than its previous close, while the Sensex plunged over 600 points to a low of 73,229.45 points. Market sentiment was weighed down by persistent selling by foreign investors and higher crude oil prices, with Brent crude rising to $111 per barrel. ALSO READ4 Small-Cap Stocks with Rising Promoter Stakes for Two Consecutive Quarters "Indian equities gave up strong early gains as elevated crude prices and continued FII selling overshadowed optimism surrounding India-US trade negotiations,” Vinod Nair, Head of Research at Geojit Investments said. FII selling, higher crude oil price Nair added that profit-booking intensified across autos, financials, metals and realty, reflecting concerns over inflation, and margin pressures, while IT showed relative resilience amid improving earnings visibility and renewed investor appetite for the sector. “Resilient Q2 earnings and robust domestic institutional flows remain important market supports, but weak breadth and persistent foreign selling point to continued caution. Near-term direction will depend on the breadth of earnings delivery, progress on trade negotiations and foreign flows, with durable moderation in crude, global yields and currency volatility crucial for market stability" Nair said. Technical view “On the daily chart, the index formed a bearish candle with an upper wick, indicating persistent selling interest at higher levels. Despite a sharp upward move during the initial minutes, the rally failed to sustain, with Nifty retreating nearly 460 points from the day’s high, highlighting strong supply at elevated levels,” Sudeep Shah, Head - Technical & Derivatives Research at SBI Securities said. “Technically, Nifty slipped below its 20-day EMA, while the RSI remained in neutral territory and the MACD stayed relatively flat. These signals suggest cooling off bullish momentum along with fresh overhead supply following the recent rally, with the index likely to consolidate until a decisive breakout establishes the next directional move,” Shah added. The 22,630–22,650 zone, corresponding to the day’s lower range, will act as the immediate support for the Nifty. A decisive breakdown below this range could drag the Nifty towards 22,500, Shah said, adding that the 22,960–22,980 zone is likely to act as an immediate hurdle on the upside. A sustained move above this range could trigger a short-covering rally towards 23,130. ALSO READIndian IT stocks rally 12% in a week – Is the turnaround sustainable? Gainers, losers Among the Nifty 50 constituents, IT stocks led the gains on Monday. Infosys ended the day 3.3% higher, HCLTech followed with 3.2% gains, Tech Mahindra with 3.1%, and TCS ended the day 2.8% higher. On the other hand, Bajaj Finance was the worst hit in the 50-stock index on Monday. Bajaj Auto, Axis Bank, Shriram Finance, Adani Enterprises, Maruti Suzuki, Trent, Eicher Motors, Eternal, and BSE closed the day over 2% lower.

docs.title: From Samosa oil to jet fuel: 7 Indian stocks set to benefit from SAF
docs.text: The oil used to fry your favourite samosa could one day help power an aircraft. What usually ends up as kitchen waste is emerging as a potential feedstock for sustainable aviation fuel (SAF), as India looks to cut aviation emissions and build alternatives to conventional jet fuel. India’s push to produce sustainable aviation fuel (SAF) from used cooking oil (UCO) is opening up opportunities across oil refining, feedstock collection, biofuel technology and engineering. Financialexpress.com spoke with a stock market expert to find out which listed entities could be under the radar and benefit from the new initiative. Key oil refinery developing sustainable aviation fuel ecosystem Indian Oil Corporation, Bharat Petroleum Corporation, Hindustan Petroleum Corporation and Mangalore Refinery And Petrochemicals are developing SAF-related projects, while Engineers India, Praj Industries and Larsen & Toubro could benefit from technology, engineering and project execution orders. However, analysts caution that the opportunity will take time to translate into meaningful earnings. Project commissioning, access to traceable feedstock, production costs and policy support will determine how quickly India’s SAF ambitions become a commercial reality. “SAF is unlikely to be a material earnings driver for IOC, BPCL, HPCL or MRPL over the next 3-5 years, as mandated volumes remain small relative to their refining capacities,” said Arun Kailasan, Research Analyst at Geojit Investments Limited. Yash Nandwani, Lead Research Analyst for the Oil and Gas sector at Nirmal Bang, similarly noted, “The opportunity is real, but is very small in earning terms for the listed O&G names.” Nandwani estimated that India would need about 65,000 tonnes of SAF in 2028, rising to about 3.8 lakh tonnes by 2030. “I therefore see SAF primarily as a compliance and strategic positioning theme rather than a material near-term earnings driver,” he said. Indian Oil Corporation: Broadest project pipeline among refiners Indian Oil is among the most advanced domestic refiners in the SAF ecosystem, with projects spanning Panipat, a HEFA joint venture at Paradip and an alcohol-to-jet partnership with LanzaJet. “IOC is best positioned, with projects spanning Panipat, Paradip and alcohol-to-jet technology that could give it a leading share of domestic SAF supply,” Kailasan said. ALSO READ57x growth in solar capacity: 2 stocks betting big on India’s next solar wave Nandwani noted that Indian Oil’s Panipat refinery was the first in India to receive ISCC CORSIA certification, in August 2025. The company has also approved a 100,000-tonne-a-year HEFA joint venture at Paradip, with an estimated cost of around Rs 1,060 crore. According to Indian Oil’s Q1 FY2026-27 investor presentation, refinery throughput stood at around 1.92 crore tonnes during the quarter. This provides context for the scale of the company’s refining operations, although the contribution from SAF will depend on actual production, feedstock costs, margins and offtake arrangements. The key milestones for the company are the commissioning of the Panipat facility, progress on the Paradip venture and approvals for the alcohol-to-jet project. Indian Oil’s ability to develop multiple production pathways could give it an advantage as the domestic market evolves. Nandwani said BPCL’s Mumbai refinery had received certification and that production was expected by the end of 2026. The timeline will be important in assessing whether the company can move from project development to sustained commercial production. For BPCL, the near-term opportunity will depend on commissioning, feedstock availability and the ability to produce certified fuel at a commercially viable cost. Analysts do not expect SAF to become a material earnings driver for the major refiners over the next three to five years, given the relatively small volumes involved. Kailasan said HPCL remained focused on demonstration and early commercial production. The company’s progress will depend on project execution, feedstock procurement and the timing of commissioning. “Investors should track SAF policy implementation, project commissioning, feedstock sourcing and airline offtake agreements to assess commercial adoption,” Kailasan said. For HPCL, confirmation of commissioning schedules and progress towards sustained production will provide a clearer indication of the opportunity than project announcements alone. As with its peers, the scale of the financial contribution will depend on production volumes and economics. He added that early access to UCO could prove advantageous as feedstock collection remains a key industry bottleneck. docs.text: Hindustan Zinc benefited from higher average prices of silver and zinc in the September 2026 quarter, and the resulting highest-ever revenue from operations along with record net profit in the quarter. Hindustan Zinc is among the world’s leading integrated Zinc producers. In addition, it is also amongst the top 10 global silver producers. Here is an insight on the factors driving the company’s record financial performance. FE Stock Insights on WhatsApPGet instant alerts on high-conviction investment themes and fundamental deep dives—direct from Financial Express.Join now The Silver Engine: How 103% Price Surge Powered 43% of Segment Earnings Hindustan Zinc sold 173 tonnes of refined silver in the second quarter of FY27, a rise of 17% y-o-y. Of equal importance, in its results presentation, the company has highlighted an average international price of silver of $ 62.6 per ounce as compared to $ 39.4 an ounce, a rise of 59% y-o-y. Global silver prices grew in the quarter on account of ‘safe haven’ status for this precious metal amidst US government debt crossing a record $ 40 trillion coupled with no signs of easing in the Middle East crisis. In the local market, average spot silver prices were nearly Rs 2.4 lakh per kilogram as compared to Rs 1.18 lakh per kg a year ago, a rise of 103% y-o-y. Part of the rise in local silver prices can be attributed to higher import duties imposed by the central government earlier this year. Silver prices had peaked at Rs 3.18 lakh in the third week of January, 2026. Hedging at $60/oz: Why Strategic Locks Cap Spot Upside Silver prices in the quarter were significantly higher on a y-o-y basis. However, in its annual report for FY26, Hindustan Zinc has highlighted that as part of its risk management framework, it undertakes strategic hedging for a portion of its annual production, within policy limits, to support greater predictability of revenues, EBITDA, and cash flows, and to mitigate adverse price movements. In line with this practice, the company hedged 59 tonnes of silver at an average price of $ 60 per troy ounce. The above position is intended to provide protection against price volatility, the company has highlighted. Hindustan Zinc sold 627 tonnes of silver in FY26. Depending on the commodity derivatives Hindustan Zinc has entered into, the company will leverage the upturn in silver prices, and it may not fully realise the rise in silver prices right away. Strong silver prices coupled with a rise in refined silver sold helped Hindustan Zinc’s silver division revenues rise 140.8% y-o-y to Rs 4,111 crore in the quarter. Also, segment profit of the silver business grew 146.5% y-o-y to Rs 3,609 crore in the quarter. docs.title: Deepak Nitrite vs Aarti vs PI Industries: Which chemical stock does Morgan Stanley prefer?
docs.text: Morgan Stanley is taking different calls on three Indian chemical companies, favouring Deepak Nitrite for its earnings recovery prospects, becoming less cautious on Aarti Industries as margins get support from chemical intermediates and fuel additives, and turning more bearish on PI Industries amid competition in its legacy agrochemical portfolio. In its October 20 report, India Chemicals: Shifting Fortunes, the brokerage argues that the sector’s prospects are diverging. Chinese supply constraints and improving agrochemical demand could help some businesses, but pricing pressure and delays in scaling newer products remain concerns for others. Deepak Nitrite leads on earnings recovery Morgan Stanley retained its ‘Overweight’ rating on Deepak Nitrite and raised its price target to Rs 1,889 from Rs 1,869. It expects improved profitability in advanced intermediates and firm phenolics margins to support an earnings recovery. The brokerage wrote: “We have also seen signs of improved volumes and pricing power in DPNT's advanced intermediates segment. The key risk to monitor is feedstock access.” The key risk is whether feedstock availability and the timing of new capacity additions allow the company to sustain its recovery. Morgan Stanley also cautioned that higher interest and depreciation costs could weigh on earnings as investments progress. Aarti Industries offers a margin recovery opportunity Morgan Stanley upgraded Aarti Industries to ‘Equal-weight’ from ‘Underweight’ and raised its price target to Rs 471 from Rs 366. It sees support from stronger monomethyl aniline (MMA) spreads, tighter supply of certain chemical intermediates in China and improved utilisation as new capacity comes on stream. The brokerage wrote: “We expect gasoline spreads to start to inflect, which should support fuel additives (such as MMA) demand.” However, Morgan Stanley stopped short of a more positive rating. It expects returns to remain constrained, while the energy business accounts for a larger share of earnings, leaving the company more exposed if refining conditions ease or fuel demand slows. PI Industries faces the toughest competitive pressure Morgan Stanley downgraded PI Industries Ltd. to relative ‘Underweight’, citing rising competition in its legacy agrochemical portfolio and a slower-than-expected transition to newer products. The brokerage expects these pressures to leave earnings vulnerable to further cuts, even if volumes improve in the second half of the financial year. ALSO READYes Bank Faces AT1 Bond Blow: Morgan Stanley Retains ‘Underweight’ The report said: “However, regulatory hurdles, adverse weather and slower-than-expected product ramp-ups have constrained volume growth relative to peers and delayed margin recovery.” The concern centres on generic competition for pyroxasulfone, a key product in PI’s legacy portfolio, and the time needed for newer agrochemicals, biologicals and pharmaceutical products to offset weaker pricing and margins. ALSO READFrom Samosa oil to jet fuel: 7 Indian stocks set to benefit from SAF How the three stocks compare MetricDeepak NitriteAarti IndustriesPI IndustriesMorgan Stanley rating‘Overweight’‘Equal-weight’‘Underweight’Price targetRs 1,889Rs 471Rs 2,030Upside / downside in report20% upside3% downside8% downsideMain positive factorAdvanced intermediates recovery and phenolics marginsMMA spreads and tighter intermediate supplyRamp-up of newer productsMain concernFeedstock access and investment executionEnergy portfolio concentration and potential easing of tailwindsGeneric competition and slow product transition Source: Morgan Stanley Research, October 20, 2026. Upside and downside figures are based on the brokerage’s report. The verdict: Deepak Nitrite stands out, while PI faces the greatest pressure Among the three, Morgan Stanley’s strongest conviction is in Deepak Nitrite, where it sees a recovery in the core businesses and support from phenolics profitability. Aarti Industries has improving margin drivers, but the brokerage remains cautious about the durability of those gains and the company’s return profile. PI Industries faces the most difficult near-term outlook as generic competition weighs on its established portfolio and newer businesses take time to scale. The report’s broader message is that chemical stocks may not move together: company-specific pricing, product mix and execution are likely to determine which businesses can turn better demand into stronger earnings.
