docs.title: Jio Platforms IPO fully subscribed in 100 minutes
docs.text: Jio Platforms’ blockbuster initial public offering (IPO) – the biggest ever at Rs 30,213 crore – got off to a flying start on Wednesday, getting fully subscribed within just 100 minutes of opening for bids. By the end of the first day, India’s biggest-ever IPO had been subscribed 3.2 times, reflecting strong investor appetite despite volatility in the secondary market. The only other IPO with over Rs 10,000 crore to received full subscription on the first day was LG Electronics. The Jio Platforms issue attracted bids for over 623 million shares worth more than Rs 69,700 crore at the upper end of the price band, against 197.53 million shares on offer. The overwhelming response was driven largely by institutional investors, who bid aggressively for a slice of the Reliance Industries-backed digital and telecom giant. ALSO READJio IPO LIVE: Issue subscribed 3 times on Day 1; QIB bids hit 9x, retail at 68% Qualified institutional buyers (QIBs) were the most aggressive in their bids, with their reserved portion subscribed 9.42 times. The category received bids for over 461.5 million shares against 49.07 million shares available. Domestic financial institutions, including banks and insurance companies, accounted for the largest chunk of demand, bidding for over 259 million shares. Foreign institutional investors were not far behind, placing bids for 161.83 million shares, while mutual funds bid for another 31.86 million shares. The response from non-institutional investors (NIIs), including high-net-worth individuals (HNIs), was also robust. The category was subscribed 1.68 times, attracting bids for 61.3 million shares against 36.44 million shares on offer. Within this segment, investors applying for more than Rs 10 lakh worth of shares subscribed 1.83 times their allotted quota, bidding for 44.48 million shares against 24.30 million shares available. HNIs accounted for 24.11 million shares of these bids. The smaller NII category, comprising applications between Rs 2 lakh and Rs 10 lakh, was subscribed 1.38 times, receiving bids for 16.79 million shares against 12.15 million shares on offer. Retail investors also pitched in by subscribing to 73% of the issue – a rare occurrence on the first day. Bids were made for 61.7 million shares against 85.04 million shares reserved for the category. Employees and shareholders also joined the subscription rush. The employee quota was subscribed 1.36 times, attracting bids for 6.4 million shares against 4.69 million shares offered. The shareholder portion was subscribed 1.46 times, with bids for 32.5 million shares against 22.34 million shares available. Several prominent market participants who had sought anchor allocations remained upbeat about the IPO’s prospects. Nikhil Kamath, co-founder of Rainmatter, which received an anchor allocation worth Rs 25 crore, disclosed on X that the investment platform had sought a much larger exposure of Rs 500 crore. Speaking to CNBC-TV18, Kamath said demand far exceeded supply and expressed confidence that the stock would make a strong market debut. Samir Arora of Helios Capital, who had also applied for an anchor allocation, was optimistic about the listing prospects. “As of now, Jio Platforms is a trade buy and post-listing, it is a growth buy,” he told CNBC-TV18. ALSO READJio IPO: Subscribe or Avoid? Check GMP, listing price prediction The strong opening followed an equally spectacular response to Jio Platforms’ Rs 8,110-crore anchor book, which had attracted bids worth around Rs 2.5 lakh crore, translating into a subscription of nearly 31 times. In dollar terms, the $26 billion anchor book as big SK Hynix’s – a South Korean semiconductor company – record breaking ADR in July 2026. With institutional demand already far exceeding the shares reserved for the category and two days of subscription still remaining, attention will now turn to whether retail participation picks up and how much further the overall subscription climbs. The IPO will remain open until October 23, with the shares expected to list on the stock exchanges on October 28.

docs.text: The GIFT Nifty indicated a cautious start for the Indian stock market on Thursday, with futures trading around 45 points lower and below the 22,700 mark in early trade. Investors will track global cues, including crude oil prices, along with domestic triggers such as second-quarter earnings, which are likely to influence market sentiment during the session. Key global and domestic cues for October 22, 2026 Asian Markets Today Asian markets saw a mixed start today. South Korea’s Kospi slipped 0.67%, while Japan’s Nikkei 225 edged up 0.19%. Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 showed little movement, remaining largely unchanged in early trade. Crude Oil Today Oil prices moved higher in early trade, with Brent crude rising 1.10% to $110.02 a barrel. US crude oil prices also gained 0.86% to $97.98 a barrel, keeping energy prices in focus for markets. ALSO READ142.1% profit growth: Why Hindustan Zinc still trades near its 52-week low US Stock Futures US stock futures were trading lower on Thursday. Dow Jones futures slipped 0.3%, down around 170 points, while S&P 500 futures fell 0.5%. Nasdaq-100 futures lost 0.7%. US Dollar Today The US Dollar Index (DXY), which measures the dollar’s value against a basket of six foreign currencies, was trading at 101.70 The index evaluates the strength or weakness of the US dollar in comparison to major currencies. The basket contains currencies such as the British Pound, Euro, Swedish Krona, Japanese Yen, Swiss Franc, etc. The Indian rupee strengthened 0.50% to close at 94.46 against the US dollar on Wednesday. US market US markets ended Wednesday’s session higher, led by gains in technology stocks. The Nasdaq Composite rose 1.05% to close at 26,702.86, while the S&P 500 gained 0.58% to settle at 7,757.17. The Dow Jones Industrial Average also advanced, adding 360.21 points, or 0.69%, to end the session at 52,856.09. Gold Rate Today In the latest trading session, COMEX gold down 0.44% to 4,131.90. The rate for 24-carat gold today is Rs 1,46,070 per 10 grams. The 18-carat gold price today in India is Rs 1,09,550. The 24-carat gold rate in Dubai today is Rs 1,46,100. Silver Rate Today In the latest trading session, COMEX silver down 0.59% to 57.37. Silver prices in India stood at Rs 249.90 per gram, while the price was Rs 2,49,900 per kilogram. ALSO READStocks to watch on Oct 22: Eternal, KEI Industries, Indian Hotels, and more FII, DII data Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) bought shares worth Rs 1,022.32 crore in the cash market on October 21, while domestic institutional investors (DIIs) recorded net purchases of Rs 1,614.32 crore. Top sectors in Wednesday’s trade The information technology sector led the gains, rising 1.83%, while artificial intelligence stocks advanced 1.6%. Digital stocks also traded higher, with the sector gaining 1.05%. Group-wise gainers and losers in Wednesday’s trade Among business groups, DCM Group led the gains, rising 5.56%, followed by HCL Group, which advanced 3.4%. Bharti Group shares also traded higher, with the group gaining 0.81%. On the losing side, Jaypee Group fell 6.52%, while Ruchi Group declined 6.33% and Jaipuria Group dropped 4.77%.

docs.title: I’m 28, earn Rs 70,000 a month and want Rs 5 crore to retire at 42. ChatGPT did the math
docs.text: I am 28, earn Rs 70,000 a month in take-home pay and live in Noida, where Rs 14,000, or 20% of my salary, goes towards rent. I expect my salary to rise by at least 10% every year and plan to increase my investments by the same percentage as my annual salary hike. But can I accumulate Rs 5 crore in 14 years and stop working completely at 42? I had earlier asked ChatGPT how I could build a Rs 2 crore retirement corpus by the age of 40 on a monthly take-home salary of Rs 70,000. This time, I raised the target to Rs 5 crore and extended my retirement timeline to age 42. ChatGPT’s projection suggested that I could reach the Rs 5 crore milestone in approximately 18 years and 10 months, around age 47, assuming a 10% annual increase in my SIP and a 15% effective annual return. That is roughly five years beyond my target retirement age of 42 I wanted a diversified investment plan that accounted for my salary, rent, expected annual hikes and the need to increase investments over time. I also wanted to know how much I would need to invest every month, how to allocate my portfolio and whether my expected salary growth would be enough to help me reach the Rs 5 crore target by the age 42. I gave ChatGPT this prompt: “Act as an expert financial advisor and investment planner in India. I am a 28-year-old salaried professional earning Rs 70,000 per month in take-home pay. I want to retire with a corpus of Rs 5 crore at 42. I am expecting a minimum double-digit salary hike every year. I also want to increase my investment portfolio by at least 10%. I am expecting a 15% annual return from investments. I stay in Noida and 20% of my salary goes in paying the rent. Suggest me a diversified investment plan to reach the target corpus.” How much of my Rs 70,000 salary can I invest? Before deciding how much to invest, I needed to calculate how much money remained after my monthly expenses. My budget is as follows: Monthly income and expensesAmountTake-home salaryRs 70,000RentRs 14,000Groceries and household essentialsRs 5,000Electricity and waterRs 2,000Internet, mobile and subscriptionsRs 1,500TransportRs 2,000Food delivery and dining outRs 5,000Personal care and household purchasesRs 3,000Insurance and medical expensesRs 2,500Family support and miscellaneous expensesRs 10,000Total monthly expensesRs 45,000Money available before investmentsRs 25,000 My listed expenses total Rs 45,000, leaving Rs 25,000 a month for investments and any additional financial needs. This represents about 35.7% of my take-home salary. ChatGPT's plan starts with a Rs 25,000 monthly systematic investment plan (SIP), or a fixed amount invested regularly. This would mean investing the entire amount left after the listed expenses. How do salary hikes and SIP increases affect the corpus? ChatGPT’s plan uses three assumptions throughout the calculation - my salary increases by 10% annually, my monthly SIP increases by 10% annually, and my investments earn an assumed 15% effective annual return. The salary hike and SIP increase are planned assumptions. The investment return is uncertain and is not a promise of what the market or any mutual fund will deliver. Under this model, my monthly SIP would rise from Rs 25,000 in the first year to about Rs 86,307 in the 14th year. My salary would also rise from Rs 70,000 to about Rs 2.42 lakh a month at the beginning of that final investment year. The projection assumes month-end SIP contributions over 14 full years, no existing investment corpus and a 10% increase in the SIP every 12 months. The calculation shows that increasing my SIP in line with my salary hikes would help me build a substantial corpus. But it would not, by itself, take me to Rs 5 crore by age 42 under these assumptions. docs.title: Why are US stock futures down? Meta, Tesla earnings and AI concerns in focus
docs.text: US stock futures fell late Wednesday as investors assessed third-quarter results from major technology companies Meta Platforms and Tesla. While Meta shares rose after reporting stronger-than-expected revenue, Tesla shares fell despite beating analysts' expectations for earnings and revenue. Dow Jones Industrial Average futures slipped 0.3%, or around 170 points. S&P 500 futures fell 0.5%, while Nasdaq-100 futures dropped 0.7%. The decline came after Wall Street ended Wednesday's regular session on a positive note. The S&P 500 recorded its third straight day of gains, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average jumped 360 points. The Nasdaq Composite closed 1% higher, helped by gains in SpaceX and Tesla during regular trading. Investors are now watching whether heavy spending on artificial intelligence (AI) can deliver enough returns to support high valuations across the technology sector. ALSO READUS banking stocks fall up to 25% in 3 months, is a bigger crisis brewing? Tesla shares fall despite earnings and revenue beat Tesla shares fell more than 3% in extended trading on Wednesday, even after the electric vehicle maker reported third-quarter earnings and revenue above analysts' expectations. The company reported adjusted earnings of 48 cents per share, compared with analysts' estimates of 45 cents per share. Revenue stood at $28.05 billion, ahead of the expected $27.92 billion, reported Investing.com. However, Tesla also cut its capital expenditure forecast for 2026 by a fifth and reported an unexpected cash surplus in the third quarter after spending less on its artificial intelligence (AI) and robotics plans than Wall Street had expected. The company now expects capital expenditure, or money spent on long-term assets and projects, to total around $20 billion in 2026, down from its earlier forecast of more than $25 billion. Tesla did not say which areas would see lower spending. In the third quarter ended September 30, Tesla spent $4.7 billion on capital expenditure, double the amount spent in the same period last year but below analysts' expectations of $7.5 billion, according to LSEG data. Tesla reported free cash flow of $1.53 billion for the quarter, against analysts' expectations of a $4.92 billion cash burn. The shares initially rose 2% in after-hours trading after the company reported positive free cash flow, higher gross margin and revenue above market expectations. However, the stock later reversed course and fell more than 3%. Investors remain concerned about whether Tesla's spending on AI, robotaxis and robotics will generate enough returns to justify the investment. While lower spending has helped the company preserve cash, it has also raised questions about whether Tesla is investing enough to deliver on its growth plans. Meta shares rise as revenue jumps 26% Meta shares rose more than 2% in extended trading after reporting stronger-than-expected revenue and giving a positive outlook for the current quarter. The company reported earnings of $3.83 per share, beating analysts' estimates of $3.57. Revenue increased 26% from a year earlier to $64.6 billion, above the market estimate of $63.34 billion, reported Investing.com. Growth in advertising and higher engagement across Meta's platforms supported its quarterly performance. However, a large legal settlement added to the company's costs during the quarter. Wall Street ends higher after SpaceX and Super Micro results Before futures turned lower in evening trading, US stocks had ended Wednesday's regular session on a positive note. SpaceX shares surged after the company reported its first profit as a publicly traded company. Investors also considered the possibility of a closer relationship between Elon Musk's SpaceX and Tesla Super Micro Computer also supported market sentiment with its results. There was also attention on Nvidia's US supply chain agreements. The chipmaker announced plans to expand its global manufacturing capacity to meet growing demand for its accelerated computing products and full-stack AI factory platform. ALSO READTop US stock picks by Indian investors: How AI chips and ETFs are reshaping portfolios The Nasdaq Composite rose 1.1% during the regular session. The S&P 500 gained 0.6%, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average ended the day 0.7% higher. Oil prices and Fed rate outlook remain in focus Investors are also keeping an eye on rising oil prices and the outlook for US interest rates. Brent crude traded above $110 a barrel during Asian trading on Thursday amid geopolitical uncertainty. Higher oil prices could add to inflation pressures, making it more difficult for the Federal Reserve to decide when to cut interest rates. Concerns about US inflation have already raised questions about the central bank's policy outlook ahead of its meeting next week. Higher interest rates can pressure stock prices, especially in the technology sector, by reducing the present value of expected future earnings. Investors await more earnings and US jobs data Investors will turn their attention to more company results on Thursday, with Procter & Gamble, Lockheed Martin, Valero Energy and Honeywell among the companies scheduled to report earnings. The economic calendar will also be in focus, with the US weekly initial jobless claims data due on Thursday morning. The figures could provide fresh clues about the health of the US labour market and influence expectations for the Federal Reserve's interest-rate decisions. Investors must conduct their own independent due diligence and seek advice from a registered financial advisor in the respective jurisdiction.

However, domestic brokerage firm Anand Rathi has maintained its ‘Buy’ rating on the stock, with a target price of ₹ 966 per share, citing reasonable valuations and favourable sector tailwinds.
The brokerage, however, believes there is still a long road ahead for HDFC Bank to catch up with ICICI Bank on key operating metrics, particularly credit growth, net interest margins (NIM) and return on equity (RoE).
According to Anand Rathi, HDFC Bank’s loan growth picked up to 16.4% year-on-year (YoY) in the September quarter of FY27 (Q2FY27). However, excluding the impact of foreign currency non-resident (FCNR-B) deposits, underlying credit growth stood at 14.4%, lagging the industry and private sector banking peers, including ICICI Bank, Axis Bank and Kotak Mahindra Bank.
Corporate and small and medium enterprise (SME) loans led growth, rising 16.4% and 23.5% YoY, respectively. Retail advances grew 12.2%, marking a recovery from six consecutive quarters of single-digit growth, partly supported by FCNR-B-linked self-leveraged loans.
Deposits increased 18.8% YoY, or 14.8% excluding FCNR-B flows. However, current account and savings account (CASA) deposits grew at a slower pace of 10.8%, pulling the CASA ratio down to 31.6%.
Anand Rathi said HDFC Bank has struggled to close the post-merger gap with ICICI Bank across key operating parameters. With CASA growth continuing to trail loan growth, the brokerage expects the bank to take longer to narrow its funding cost gap with ICICI Bank.
Consequently, it does not expect HDFC Bank’s loan growth or RoE to sustainably exceed 15% over the medium term.
Anand Rathi has reiterated its ‘Buy’ rating on HDFC Bank, with a sum-of-the-parts (SOTP)-based target price of ₹ 966 per share. The brokerage values the bank’s core business at 1.8 times its estimated price-to-adjusted book value (P/ABV) for FY29 and assigns ₹ 100 per share to its subsidiaries.
According to the brokerage, the stock’s sharp correction has made its valuation reasonable, while favourable sector tailwinds provide support to the investment case. However, the recovery in operating performance may take time, given the challenges in closing the gap with ICICI Bank on credit growth, margins and funding costs.
For investors, the key factors to watch will be the sustainability of loan growth, a recovery in net interest margins, improvement in low-cost deposit mobilisation and the impact of leadership changes on business continuity, according to the brokerage firm.
HDFC Bank’s share price has remained under pressure across multiple timeframes, reflecting sustained weakness in the stock. The shares have declined 1.55% over the past week and 5.39% over the past month.
The stock has fallen 29.41% year-to-date (YTD) and 30.57% over the past year, highlighting the extent of the correction. The weakness has also extended over the longer term, with HDFC Bank shares declining 8.11% over three years and 16.52% over five years.

docs.title: Buy Bajaj Finance Ltd for the Target Rs.1,250 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
Operationally strong; capital raise will offset organic NIM pressure 
 NIM (calc.) contracted ~9bp QoQ; gold loan slippages are transitory in nature 
* Bajaj Finance’s (BAF) 2QFY27 PAT grew 29% YoY to ~INR63.7b (in line). NII in 2QFY27 grew 24% YoY to ~INR133.3b (in line). Non-interest income stood at ~INR26.4b (up 11% YoY). Opex grew ~23% YoY to ~INR52.7b (in line). PPoP stood at INR107b (in line) and grew 21% YoY.
* Credit costs stood at ~INR21.7b (in line). Annualized credit costs were broadly stable QoQ at ~1.56% (PQ: ~1.54% and PY: ~2.05%). 2QFY27 includes a prudent management overlay of INR3.4b for macroeconomic risks. Excluding this provision, credit costs declined 12% YoY to INR18.3b, translating into ~1.32%.
* BAF highlighted that the vintage credit performance across 3MOB, 6MOB, and 9MOB continues to reflect significant improvement. Management remains optimistic on the FY27 credit cost outlook, expecting full-year credit costs to remain within the 1HFY27 range, supported by improving portfolio performance, proactive underwriting, and prudent overlays. We model credit costs of ~1.5% each in FY27/FY28.
* BAF upgraded its FY27 AUM growth guidance to 26-27%, supported by improving traction across business segments, while reiterating its long-term growth guidance of 23-25%. Growth momentum remained strong across segments, except MSME, where management expects growth to recover to double-digit levels in 2HFY27. We model AUM growth of 26% over FY26-28E. Management shared that it has submitted its feedback on the proposed RBI restrictions on revolving credit and expects a balanced framework, as a complete ban could temporarily impact AUM, NIMs, and profitability. On proposed insurance commission changes, the company is evaluating options to mitigate the impact on fee income and margins.
* BAF has moved beyond earnings normalization and is entering a phase of structurally stronger earnings growth. The combination of strong loan growth, operating efficiencies to offset margin pressure, improving asset quality, and declining credit costs are expected to drive a meaningful acceleration in profitability.
* We raise our FY27/FY28 EPS estimates by ~1%/4%, factoring in stronger AUM growth and benefit on NIM from the proposed equity capital raise of ~INR175b, which we expect to be completed by Dec’26. We model PAT CAGR of ~30% over FY26-FY28E and RoA/RoE of 4.1%/20% in FY28E. We reiterate our BUY rating on the stock with a TP of INR1,250 (premised on 4x Sep’28E BVPS). Key risks:
1) Potential asset quality deterioration due to weak monsoons, El Nino, and elevated oil prices
2) impact on AUM growth and NIM pressure if the RBI’s proposed restrictions on revolving credit are implemented in their current form
3) lower fee income due to proposed IRDAI regulations on insurance commissions
 Strong and broad-based AUM growth; NIM (calc.) contracts ~9bp QoQ 
 * Total AUM grew 26.5% YoY/6.9% QoQ to INR5.85t. QoQ AUM growth was driven by Gold Loans (+14%), Rural Sales Finance (+7%), Consumer Sales Finance (~6%), LAS (~15%), MFI (~8%), and Car Loans (+6%).
* New customer acquisition stood at ~4.4m in 2QFY27. BAF targets 60-62m new loans and 18-20m customer additions to its franchise in FY27. Management indicated that FY27 (organic) NIM contraction could be marginally higher than the initial 10-15bp guidance, driven by an expected increase in funding costs in 3Q/4QFY27 in a rising interest rate cycle. We expect BAF to deliver ~26% AUM CAGR over FY26-28, with NIM of ~9.7%/9.6% in FY27E/FY28E. (FY26: 9.7%).
 Minor deterioration in asset quality; credit costs stable QoQ 
* As of Sep’26, GNPA and NNPA stood at 1.06% (increased ~10bp QoQ) and 0.42% (increased ~3bp QoQ), respectively, as of Sep’26. PCR on Stage 3 assets was broadly stable QoQ at ~60%.
* Stage 2 and 3 assets increased ~INR16b in 2QFY27, including ~INR10.5b increase in Stage 2 gold loan due to short-tenor schemes that are no longer being offered. The company does not expect the transitional increase in Stage 2 gold loans to impact credit costs. Adjusting for this transient movement, S2 and S3 loans improved to 1.88% of loans from 1.90% in 1QFY27.
 Highlights from the management commentary 
* BAF is closely monitoring early-vintage performance and tightening originations where 3MOB metrics indicate emerging stress. Self-employed unsecured borrowers are viewed as more vulnerable to inflation and elevated oil prices, with stress testing prompting additional Stage 1 and Stage 2 provisions for nonsalaried unsecured borrowers amid risks from El Nino, monsoons, and oil prices.
* The company discontinued short-tenor schemes in August and is reverting to longer-tenor products of 12 months, with options for monthly or quarterly interest payments. Around 55% of the elevated Stage 2 balance has already been resolved, with no material credit cost or auction impact expected.
* BAF delivered a healthy quarter, with broad-based growth across segments and continued improvement in asset quality, supported by strong vintage performance and stable credit costs. While there was some marginal asset quality deterioration, largely driven by gold loans, management remains confident of negligible ultimate credit losses. Margins declined during the quarter and could witness further (organic) contraction due to expected rise in borrowing costs.
* BAF trades at 3.3x FY28E P/BV and ~19x P/E (after incorporating the expected equity capital raise through QIP and preferential allotment of warrants). We model a PAT CAGR of ~30% over FY26-FY28E and RoA/RoE of 4.1%/20% in FY28E. We believe the company is entering a phase of sustainable earnings compounding, driven by broad-based growth, resilient profitability, and improving asset quality. We reiterate our BUY rating on the stock with a TP of INR1,250 (premised on 4x Sep’28E BVPS).

docs.title: Buy Piramal Finance Ltd for the Target Rs 2,470 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
Levers in place to improve profitability; guidance intact Asset quality stable; potential impact on insurance commissions manageable 
* Piramal Finance (Piramal)’s 2QFY27 PAT rose 67% YoY to ~INR5.45b (in line). NII rose 42% YoY to ~INR14.5b in 2Q (in line). Other income grew ~3% YoY to INR3.2b (~15% miss).
* Credit costs dipped to ~INR303m (vs. MOFSLe of ~INR473m), led by write-backs from the legacy wholesale portfolio. This translated into credit costs of ~1.1% for 2QFY27 (PQ: 1.8%; PY: 1.1%). PPOP grew ~64% YoY to ~INR8.5b (~10% miss).
* Piramal expects margins to gradually improve to ~6.8%, driven by a favorable business mix, declining CoB, and the continued run-down of the legacy book, which now accounts for ~1.5% of total AUM. The increasing share of unsecured lending, targeted to reach 25-26% of AUM (from 21% currently), should support portfolio yields. The refinancing of maturing higher-cost debt at a lower cost of ~8.4-8.5% and the upgrade in its credit ratings to AA+, will help it manage its borrowing costs better (relative to peers) in a rising interest rate cycle. We expect Piramal’s NIM to improve to 5.3%/5.6% in FY27E/FY28E (FY26: 4.7%), also partly aided by the equity raise in 1HFY27.
* Piramal’s target of achieving a 2.5% RoAUM by 4QFY27 is underpinned by operating leverage, a favorable business mix, and lower funding costs. The company’s calibrated expansion in higher-yielding unsecured lending, supported by granular risk-based underwriting and healthy asset quality, should enable growth while maintaining credit discipline. The execution of these strategic priorities will be key to driving a sustained improvement in profitability and delivering the company’s medium-term return aspirations.
* The stock currently trades at ~1.3x FY28E P/BV. We estimate an AUM CAGR of ~28% and a PAT CAGR of 48% over FY26-FY28, with an RoA/RoE of 2.5%/10.4% in FY28E. We reiterate our BUY rating on the stock with a TP of INR2,470 (based on Sep’28E SoTP; refer to Exhibit 1).
 Sustained growth momentum; AUM targeted to double by FY28 
* Total AUM grew 24% YoY and ~6% QoQ to INR1.13t. Wholesale 2.0 AUM grew ~24% YoY to INR140b while Wholesale 1.0 AUM declined to INR17b. The growth-to-legacy AUM mix has improved to 98.5%:1.5% in Sep’26.
* Retail AUM grew ~30% YoY to INR975b with its share in the loan book remaining stable sequentially at ~86%. Retail disbursements grew ~34% YoY to INR146b.
* Piramal aims to sustain strong growth, targeting ~25% AUM expansion in FY27 and doubling AUM every three years, implying a loan book of INR1.5t by FY28. Growth is expected to be driven by its expanding customer base of ~6.5m, deeper penetration and cross-selling, which contributes ~30% of unsecured disbursements and offers lower operating costs and better credit risk metrics than open-market sourcing. We expect Piramal to deliver an AUM CAGR of ~28% over FY26-28
 Asset quality holds firm; underwriting remains disciplined 
* GS3 remained stable QoQ at ~2.4% while NS3 increased ~10 bp QoQ to ~1.7%. Stage 3 PCR remained stable QoQ at ~31.4%.
* Retail business 90+ dpd remained stable QoQ at 0.7% (PY: 0.8%). Growth business credit costs declined to ~1.5% (PQ: 1.6%).
* Piramal maintained stable and healthy asset quality across its retail and wholesale businesses, with credit decisions in unsecured lending guided by subsegment-level risk and delinquency trends. While the company continues to monitor stress among home loan customers employed in the IT sector in South India, the stress has not spread to adjacent customer segments. Similarly, the weak monsoon has not materially affected agricultural-income customers, with bounce rates remaining stable sequentially and below 2QFY26 levels. We expect credit costs to moderate to 1.4%/1.6% for FY27E/FY28E (vs ~2.9% in FY26).
 Highlights from the management commentary 
* Piramal indicated that implementation of the IRDAI consultation paper in its current form from Apr’27 could reduce insurance commissions, resulting in an estimated gross impact of ~18-24bp on FY28 RoA. Any improvement in Pramerica Life Insurance's economics would flow proportionately back to Piramal Finance through consolidation, providing a natural offset to the potential reduction in commissions.
* Prepayments in the wholesale business remained elevated, with the company receiving INR18.9b during the quarter, equivalent to ~72% of disbursements.
* Piramal delivered a healthy operational performance in 2QFY27, with a 30% YoY rise in its Growth business AUM and a 69% YoY decline in the legacy book, which now accounts for just ~1.5% of total AUM. Business momentum remained strong across secured and unsecured lending, supported by an expanding customer franchise and stable asset quality. Continued operating efficiencies, stable borrowing costs, and a favorable business mix are expected to drive profitability, with the company retaining its target of achieving RoAUM of 2.5% in the Growth business by 4QFY27.
* We estimate an AUM CAGR of ~28% and a PAT CAGR of 48% over FY26-FY28, with an RoA/RoE of 2.5%/10.4% in FY28E. We reiterate our BUY rating on the stock with a TP of INR2,470 (based on Sep’28E SoTP; refer to Exhibit 1)

docs.title: Buy Ellenbarrie Industrial Gases Ltd for the Target Rs 420 by Motilal Oswal Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
Capturing India’s structural growth in industrial gases 
Ellenbarrie Industrial Gases (ELLEN) is one of India’s leading industrial gas manufacturers, supplying oxygen, nitrogen, argon and carbon dioxide to key enduser industries, including steel, healthcare, pharmaceuticals and manufacturing, through on-site and merchant supply models. We believe ELLEN is well positioned to benefit from the structural growth in India’s domestic solar cell manufacturing ecosystem and the expansion of the steel and pharmaceutical industries.
* ELLEN is expanding its presence in high-value solar manufacturing applications through ultra-high-purity gases, with its upcoming central India facility (FY28) set to supply ammonia and nitrous oxide to capitalize on the sector’s growth.
* India’s crude steel capacity is projected to reach 604 MT by CY47, which presents a significant growth opportunity for ELLEN. The recently commercialized 320 TPD on-site plant in East India, backed by a long-term steel supply contract, along with planned capacity expansions, positions the company well to capitalize on rising industrial gas demand.
* Further, India’s growing prominence as a pharmaceutical manufacturing hub, supported by cost competitiveness, supply-chain diversification from China and government initiatives such as PLI schemes and Ayushman Bharat, is expected to drive industrial gas demand, creating growth opportunities for ELLEN.
* We expect ELLEN to clock a CAGR of 40%/36%/26% in revenue/EBITDA/ PAT during FY26-29. We value the company based on 30x Sep’28 EPS. Reiterate BUY with a TP of INR420.
 Positioning for growth in India’s solar manufacturing ecosystem 
* ELLEN is strengthening its presence in emerging sectors such as solar manufacturing by supplying application-specific gases, including ultrahigh-purity gases (99.9999% purity), while expanding its capabilities to serve higher-value applications.
* India’s solar cell manufacturing industry is poised for further growth, with ALMM-listed solar cell manufacturing capacity reaching ~37.8 GW as of Oct’26. The total capacity is expected to reach to ~56.6 GW in FY27 and ~64.3GW in FY28.
* Domestic solar cell manufacturing will be supported by government initiatives such as the production-linked incentive (PLI) scheme, mandatory sourcing of approved list of models and manufacturers (ALMM), the extension of ALMM requirements to ingots and wafers from Jun’28, and domestic content requirement (DCR) mandates under the PM Surya Ghar, PM-KUSUM and CPSU schemes. These factors will also strengthen local solar supply chain, including locally manufactured industrial gasses, which are one of the key inputs for solar cell.
* Solar cell manufacturing requires ultra-high-purity oxygen, which commands significantly higher realizations than conventional oxygen, nitrogen and argon, along with high-purity ammonia and nitrous oxide.
* To capture the opportunity, ELLEN is installing a new plant in central India, which will be strategically located near a major solar cell manufacturing hub and will supply key industrial gasses for the manufacturing of solar cells. The upcoming facility is expected to be operational by FY28.
 Positioned to benefit from long-term steel industry growth 
* The steel industry is a key end-market for ELLEN, accounting for ~31% of FY26 revenue. Oxygen is used for decarburization, while argon supports stirring and refining, and nitrogen is used for inerting and oxygen-enrichment applications.
* India's crude steel capacity is expected to increase at a CAGR of 4.9% from 220MT in FY26 to 604MT in FY47. Considering this, ELLEN focuses on expanding its capacity to capture the growing demand from the steel sector. Ellen has recently commercialized its 320 TPD on-site plant in East India with revenue contribution starting from Sep’26, supported by a long-term steel supply contract.
* The ramp-up at the Kurnool and Uluberia 2 merchant plants is progressing well, with continued focus on improving capacity utilization through FY27.
* ELLEN operates through a diversified portfolio of gases, supported by long-term contracts that ensure stable demand and customer retention. Its balanced business model across bulk, packaged, and onsite supplies contributed 68%, 15%, and 16% of revenue in FY26, respectively.
* Ellen is expected to sustain its growth momentum, aided by the mid- to longterm triggers such as
1) capacity expansion across India, especially In North and Central India to capture the opportunity in these markets
2) development of domestic solar cell manufacturing ecosystem and capturing opportunities in solar cell industry
3) stable demand from well-diversified core industries
4) ramp-up of newly commercialized plants.
* We expect ELLEN to clock a CAGR of 40%/36%/26% in revenue/EBITDA/ PAT during FY26-29. We value the company based on 30x Sep’28 EPS. Reiterate BUY with a TP of INR420.

docs.text:
HZL (~90% of VEDL’s EBITDA) beat our/consensus’ 2Q estimates, with reported EBITDA at Rs92.9bn (+14.2% qoq) as zinc CoP fell to $703/t from $851/t. Net cash stood at Rs112.7bn after a record FCF of Rs62.0bn. Management cut its FY27 guidance for CoP to $825-850/t, kept its 680t silver production target, while remaining constructive on Zn and Ag given supply deficits. We believe the recent Ag price correction is a near-term risk, which should though be offset by higher volumes; also, spot prices point to further upside. We maintain BUY and TP of Rs350.
 Further improvement in CoP led to the 2Q EBITDA beat 
VEDL’s subsidiary HZL, contributing ~90% of its consolidated EBITDA, logged a strong 2Q with reported EBITDA at Rs92.9bn, beating our and consensus’ estimate (6.9% vs Emkay; 9.2% vs consensus). EBITDA growth remained strong, increasing 14.2% qoq, mainly driven by lower zinc CoP ($703/t vs $851/t in 1Q), which was supported by higher sulfuric acid realizations during 2Q; this was further backed by the sequentially higher volumes across silver and lead—which increased 16.1% and 8.5% qoq, respectively, and the INR depreciation. Consequently, HZL saw strong performance despite lower hedging realization vs quarterly average, with EBITDA margin remaining robust at 61.3%. Thus, PAT rose to Rs64.1bn (vs Rs54.7 in 1Q), driven by strong operating leverage. HZL generated a record FCF of Rs62.0bn, ending 2Q with net cash of Rs112.7bn.
 Healthy production and cost guidance keeps earnings momentum intact 
Management reiterated confidence in achieving its 680t silver production guidance, with ~340t delivered in 1H (including sale of 10kt lead concentrate containing 10t of silver, in 2Q), supported by absence of any major maintenance shutdowns for remaining FY27. HZL reduced zinc CoP guidance to $825-850/t for the full year from $975-1,000/t, also highlighting that elevated sulfuric acid prices and higher production could provide additional cost tailwinds. The company remains constructive on the medium-term outlook for both zinc and silver, given the supply-demand imbalance in both markets. We believe strong production volumes and supportive zinc prices will continue supporting earnings momentum during 2HFY27. While the recent correction in the price of silver could weigh on silver earnings in the near term, we expect this headwind to be largely offset by higher silver volumes over coming quarters
 Strong 2Q numbers to lead FY27E earnings upgrade; maintain BUY We expect HZL to log a robust FY27E EBITDA at Rs302bn (~90% of VEDL's EBITDA) backed by strong margin visibility driven by favorable Zn and Ag prices—now 23% and 28% above the FY26 average level, respectively. Should spot prices sustain at $3,731/t for Zn and $58/oz for Ag, earnings could see further upside. Coupled with HZL's firstquartile position on the global zinc cost curve, we remain constructive on its earnings and growth outlook. Accordingly, we maintain BUY on VEDL with unchanged TP of Rs350.

docs.title: Buy UltraTech Cement Ltd for the Target Rs 13,200 by Emkay Global Financial Services Ltd
docs.text:
UltraTech Cement (UTCEM) reported consolidated EBITDA of ~Rs37bn (up 20% yoy), in line with our and street estimates. Domestic grey cement volumes grew ~14% yoy, well ahead of industry growth of ~9%, while grey realization dipped <1% qoq (up ~2% yoy) on softer Jul/Aug-26. Unit operating cost rose ~8% qoq (Rs370/t), primarily due to higher RM + fuel costs (Rs210) and the balance owing to negative operating leverage. However, blended realizations increased by ~2% sequentially (~Rs130/t) led by ~30%/~50% growth in RMC/building material, respectively. Consequently, EBITDA/t stood at Rs974 (Emkay: Rs980) vs Rs914 in 2QFY26 and Rs1,214 in 1QFY27. Our view: UTCEM demonstrated strong volume growth and healthy margin profile in a challenging quarter. Going ahead, we expect an improving margin trajectory, as the industry realizes operating leverage benefits (2H), aided by cement price hikes taken during early 3QFY27 (spot prices up ~5% vs 2Q average). UTCEM remains our top pick, given its purchasing power (read scale) and strengthening market-share position amid a volatile environment. We broadly maintain our estimates and continue to value UTCEM at 17x Sep-28E EV/EBITDA while raising TP by ~2% to Rs13,200 (from Rs13,000). The stock trades at ~14x 1YF EV/EBITDA, akin to the trough seen during the Russia-Ukraine war. Hence, we consider UTCEM as a safe bet on risk-reward ratio; maintain BUY.
 Robust volumes and stable pricing offset rising costs 
UTCEM’s consolidated revenue grew ~19% yoy (down ~6% qoq) to ~Rs233bn, driven by ~13% volume growth. Capacity utilization improved to 71% from ~66% in 2QFY26 (on higher capacity base). Grey realization was broadly stable (down <1% qoq), as soft Jul/Aug-26 offset healthy recovery in Sep-26. On the cost front, unit variable cost rose ~6% on both yoy and qoq basis (Rs210), due to inflation in unit (RM+P&F) cost (up ~8%/9% yoy/qoq). Blended fuel rate climbed to Rs2.09/mcal from Rs1.90 in 1QFY27, despite cutting pet coke usage by 11pps qoq. Fixed cost/t jumped ~15% qoq (flat yoy) on operating de-leverage, taking unit operating cost up ~Rs370/t qoq. PAT grew ~21% yoy to ~Rs15bn, ~6% below our estimate, due to higher interest cost on issuance of fresh NCDs.
 Marching toward 240mtpa with a resilient balance sheet 
UTCEM commissioned 4.6mtpa in Sep-26, taking consolidated capacity to ~210mtpa. The company remains on track to reach >240mtpa by FY28-end and will announce its next phase of organic expansion by FY27-end. The management retained FY27 capex guidance at ~Rs100bn. In 1HFY27, the company generated OCF of ~Rs69bn (up ~24% yoy), and spent ~Rs57bn on capex, resulting in FCF of ~Rs12bn. The ~Rs70bn dividend payout was thus largely funded through ~Rs54bn of fresh borrowings (including Rs50bn of NCD). As a result, net debt rose to ~Rs235bn (vs ~Rs166bn in Mar-26), raising net debt/EBITDA to ~1.3x from ~0.9x; management expects it to fall below 1x by Mar-27.

docs.title: Vedanta Shares: Should You Buy After Hindustan Zinc Beats Q2 Estimates? Emkay Keeps Buy and a Rs 350 Target
docs.text:
Emkay Global kept its Buy rating on Vedanta with an unchanged target of Rs 350 after subsidiary Hindustan Zinc reported a 142% rise in Q2 FY27 profit to Rs 6,412 crore on 19 Oct 2026. Vedanta shares traded at Rs 236.85 on 21 Oct (down 2.61%), so the target is about 47.8% above the price (my calculation). Hindustan Zinc itself opened about 4% higher on 21 Oct and then fell to Rs 525.00, down 2.49%. Emkay's valuation method was not stated in the report I read, and the target is a broker view and not a promise.
Vedanta shares are rated Buy by Emkay Global with an unchanged target price of Rs 350, kept after Hindustan Zinc reported Q2 FY27 net profit of Rs 6,412 crore, up 142% from Rs 2,649 crore, and a record EBITDA of about Rs 9,285 crore. Emkay says Hindustan Zinc is about 90% of Vedanta's FY27 EBITDA, so the earnings beat feeds straight into Vedanta, and it sees more upside if zinc and silver prices stay near spot levels. At Rs 236.85 on 21 Oct the Emkay target is about 47.8% above the price (my calculation), but Vedanta shares fell 2.61% on the day even after the results, and the report did not state how the target was valued. Whether to buy depends on your view of zinc and silver prices, the group's structure and your own risk limit, so treat the call as one input and not as advice.
Vedanta shares moved lower on 21 Oct 2026 even though the main earnings driver, Hindustan Zinc, posted a record quarter. Hindustan Zinc's Q2 FY27 results on 19 Oct showed profit up 142%, revenue up about 77% and a zinc production cost that fell 29% year on year, and the stock opened about 4% higher on Wednesday before selling off.
This article on Vedanta shares covers the Hindustan Zinc results, Emkay's Buy call and what it assumes, how Vedanta shares and Hindustan Zinc trade today, the other broker views, the risks and what to check before you buy. It is educational and not a recommendation to buy or sell any share.

The two reports I read give different revenue figures and a slightly different margin (62% against 61.3%), so check the filing for the exact numbers behind the Vedanta shares story. The company credited higher metal prices, higher output, better by-product realisation and a stronger dollar. Silver sales more than doubled, which shows how much the result depends on one by-product.

The 90% share is a useful cross-check. The data I pulled shows Vedanta's June 2026 quarter EBITDA at Rs 9,043 crore, and Hindustan Zinc's June quarter EBITDA works out to about Rs 8,130 crore (my calculation from the Q2 figure and the 14.2% quarterly growth), which is also about 90%. That fits Emkay's view that Vedanta shares are now mostly a Hindustan Zinc play. I did not find Vedanta's own September-quarter result in the data, so Emkay's view of the parent's numbers is not something I could check.
 Download the Univest iOS App or Univest Android App to open a demat account and track metal stocks. 
 Risk: A target of Rs 350 depends on zinc and silver prices that are 23% and 28% above last year's average, so a fall in either would cut the earnings Emkay builds on.
Both stocks opened higher and sold off, which suggests that traders used the gap up to book profit. Hindustan Zinc's open at Rs 559.85 sat right at the Rs 557 to Rs 560 resistance that KC Securities named (my reading). The data provider also shows Vedanta at a P/E of 3.33 and a dividend yield near 14%, but those figures probably mix pre-demerger earnings and dividends with the new share price, so I do not rely on them for Vedanta shares. Several group companies now trade separately, including Vedanta Aluminium Metal at Rs 355.80, Vedanta Power at Rs 30.30 and Vedanta Oil and Gas at Rs 29.19, and all fell more than 4% on the day.
 Risk: Since Vedanta shares now rest mostly on one subsidiary, a weak day in Hindustan Zinc, as on 21 Oct, shows up directly in the parent.
Systematix raised its FY27 EBITDA estimate for Hindustan Zinc by 23% and FY28 by 9%. Its Rs 677 target is about 29% above Rs 525 (my calculation), and the company's guidance for FY27 zinc cost of production was cut to $825 to $850 a tonne from $975 to $1,000. Silver production guidance for FY27 is 680 tonnes, rising to about 730 to 750 tonnes in FY28. These estimates sit behind the cost and volume trend that supports Vedanta shares.
The positives for Vedanta shares are clear: record profit at the main subsidiary, a falling cost base and a broker who sees about 47.8% upside. The cautions are just as clear. The stock fell on the day of good news, the cost level in Q2 is below management's own guidance for the year and metal prices drive most of the profit. A buyer should decide in advance how much loss to accept.
Vedanta shares carry a Buy rating from Emkay with an unchanged Rs 350 target after Hindustan Zinc's record Q2 FY27, but they fell 2.61% to Rs 236.85 on 21 Oct. The upside is large on paper at about 47.8%, yet the valuation method is unknown and the profit leans on metal prices. Read the filings, track zinc and silver and size any position to your own risk.

Pricing recovery and operating leverage to support earnings; cost inflation remains a near-term monitorable 
We maintain our ‘BUY’ rating on UltraTech Cement (UTCEM) , with a TP of INR 15,210/share, supported by its industry-leading scale, cost competitiveness and long-term growth visibility. Despite near-term margin pressure from elevated fuel cost, strong volume growth and improving pricing momentum are expected to support an earnings recovery in H2FY27. Sustained price realisation and EBITDA/t improvement remain key to our thesis.
(1) Improving pricing momentum, with October spot realisation ~5% above the Q2FY27 average, supporting potential Q3 earnings recovery
(2) Strong volume growth, with Q2FY27 volumes up 12.9% YoY and capacity utilisation at 71%, reflecting market-share gains (especially in South market)
(3) UTCEM reiterated its target of achieving INR 1,400/t EBITDA by March 2028, but we have incorporated ~1,300/t
(4) Long-term growth visibility, supported by infrastructure spending, urban housing and capacity expansion towards 240 MTPA. We believe UTCEM is bestpositioned to benefit from an industry upcycle, given its scale, extensive market reach and capacity expansion.
However, we remain cautious about fuel-cost inflation and the sustainability of price hike. Fuel cost rose, from INR 45/bag in Q1FY27 to INR 51.5/bag in Q2FY27. While price hike should support margins, recovery hinges on sustained realisations and demand normalisation, with further cost escalation posing a key downside risk.
We estimate EBITDA to expand at a 14.0% CAGR over FY26–FY29E, supported by volume growth, operating efficiencies and acquisition synergies. We value UTCEM using an EV/CE methodology, applying a 3.8x FY28E EV/CE multiple to arrive at our one-year TP of INR 15,210/share. While our premium valuation reflects UTCEM's structural advantages, delivery of the anticipated earnings recovery remains critical. We retain UTCEM as our preferred large-cap cement play, with Q3FY27 pricing and margin performance being key monitorables.
 Q2FY27 result: Strong volume growth amid cost headwinds 
UTCEM reported Q2FY27 consolidated revenue and EBITDA of INR 232.9 Bn (+18.8% YoY, -5.5% QoQ) and INR 37.2 Bn (+20.3% YoY, - 25.8% QoQ) vs CIE estimate of INR 220.3 Bn and INR 34.5 Bn, respectively. Total volume for Q2 stood at 38.2 Mnt (including Kesoram & India Cement) (vs CIE est. 37.3 Mnt), up 12.9% YoY.
Realisation/t came in at INR 6,095/t (+5.2% YoY and +2.2% QoQ), which is higher than CIE’s est. of INR 5,907/t. Total cost/t came in at INR 5,121/t (+5.0% YoY and +7.8% QoQ), which is higher than CIE est of INR 4,982/t. As a result, EBITDA/t came in at INR 974/t (vs CIE est. INR 925/t), up 6.5% YoY and down 19.8% QoQ.
